### S-04 · high · partial (security) · effort S
**Demo seed publishes a shared password, including for the platform operator**

- Sources: audit:S-04, security:H-1, docs:DOC-4
- Detail: [audit:S-04] seed.ts L56, L109-L117, L127: every seeded account, including operator@cyclowareness.com with role super_admin, gets the same shared password, which is printed in .env.example and the README demo-account table. The demo tenant switches mandatory admin 2FA off; the operator role always requires 2FA but the seeded operator has none yet, so whoever knows the password is sent to enrol their own authenticator (profile.ts L24-L34 needs only the password). The seed truncates every table when ALLOW_SEED=1, which the docker-compose seed service sets unconditionally. Any seeded instance reachable from the internet (CLAUDE.md mentions a presentation copy on port 3100) can be taken over at platform-operator level: every tenant, plan switches and admin reset links.
  [security:H-1] portal/.env.example:89 sets SEED_PASSWORD to the published value and the seed hashes it into ~37 accounts including operator@cyclowareness.com (super_admin) and the demo tenant admin; the repository is public on GitHub. The operator has no second factor until first sign-in, so an attacker enrols their own authenticator and controls every tenant. Branch fix (seed-data.ts): `export const PUBLISHED_SEED_PASSWORD = "<published value>"; export function seedPasswordProblem(e) { if (!e.DATABASE_URL && e.NODE_ENV !== "production") return null; ... if (!password || password === PUBLISHED_SEED_PASSWORD) return "SEED_PASSWORD is unset or is the demo password published..."; if (password.length < 12) return "...at least 12 characters..."; return null; }` and seed.ts: `const passwordProblem = seedPasswordProblem(process.env); if (passwordProblem) { console.error(`Refusing to seed: ${passwordProblem}`); process.exit(1); }`; the fallback becomes `process.env.SEED_PASSWORD ?? PUBLISHED_SEED_PASSWORD`. .env.example and README (3 places) now say the published value works only for the local embedded database. The local PGlite path keeps the default, so the owner's :3100 presentation copy and the demo branch's demo.mjs (runs `npm run db:reset` without DATABASE_URL/NODE_ENV=production, so the guard passes) still use the published password: rotation is the owner's job, not the code's.
  [docs:DOC-4] README Quick start line 197: 'The password for all of them is the SEED_PASSWORD value in portal/.env.example' followed by a table of eight accounts (line 199-208) including operator@cyclowareness.com (platform operator). portal/.env.example line with SEED_PASSWORD= is committed (presence confirmed, value not printed). The security branch reports the repository is public, so any internet-reachable instance seeded with the example file (presentation copy on :3100, previews) is operator-level accessible; the security branch adds a seed guard, but the docs branch README still advertises the path to the password.
- Evidence: Main: portal/scripts/seed.ts:56 `const SEED_PASSWORD = process.env.SEED_PASSWORD ?? "<published literal>"` (the same value as portal/.env.example:86, committed); seed.ts:114 hashes it for operator@cyclowareness.com with role super_admin (seed.ts:106-115, no totpSecret, so totpEnabled stays false); seed.ts:170 for every other person; seed.ts:127 `settings.identity.requireAdmin2fa = false` for the demo tenant. portal/docker-compose.yml:100 sets `ALLOW_SEED: "1"` unconditionally on the seed service. The take-over path is real: permissions.ts:84-85 makes 2FA mandatory for super_admin, auth.ts:194 opens the session with twoFactorVerified=true when totpEnabled is false, viewer.ts:166 (requirePermission) redirects the operator to /profile?section=security&required=1, and profile.ts:24-34 startTotpAction enrols an authenticator on the strength of the password alone. portal/README.md:61,72,120,198 point at the password. Root README.md on main is EMPTY (0 lines); the 'README line 197' table is added by the docs branch (docs.diff:204,215) and the demo branch (demo.diff:1). Owner's :3100 copy: .claude/launch.json:16-23 runs scratchpad/demo/launch-demo.mjs = `next start -p 3100` (binds every interface by default) from a copy whose .env.local sets no SEED_PASSWORD (key names checked, values not read), so it was seeded with the published default. Security branch (security.diff:547-615): seed-data.ts exports PUBLISHED_SEED_PASSWORD + seedPasswordProblem(), seed.ts:42-47 refuses the published/short/missing value when DATABASE_URL or NODE_ENV=production is set, tests/seed-guard.test.ts (security.diff:845-873), .env.example and portal/README.md wording. It leaves the local PGlite path (and therefore :3100, which runs the embedded database) on the published literal; demo branch demo.mjs runs `npm run db:reset` with no DATABASE_URL (demo.diff hunk line 112) but binds 127.0.0.1 only (`const host = "127.0.0.1"`).
- Smallest fix: Land the security branch's guard, then one more step so the literal leaves the repository: in portal/scripts/seed.ts:56 replace the fallback with `process.env.SEED_PASSWORD || randomToken(12)` (randomToken is already imported from ../src/server/services/progress) and print the generated value once in the final console.log at seed.ts:897; delete PUBLISHED_SEED_PASSWORD from seed-data.ts (seedPasswordProblem then only checks length) and set `SEED_PASSWORD=` empty in portal/.env.example:86 with the comment 'leave empty to get a random one printed by the seed'; update portal/README.md:61,120,198 and the docs-branch README table (docs.diff:204) to say 'printed by npm run setup'. Keep the operator in the seed (the docker bootstrap invitation at portal/README.md:195 is the production path).

### TST-1 · high · fixed_on_branch (tests) · effort S
**Passwords built from the person's own name or email were accepted**

- Sources: tests:TST-1
- Detail: Root cause (diff, portal/src/lib/password-strength.ts): checkPassword() passed userInputs ([email, name]) straight to zxcvbn's factory.check(); zxcvbn matches a user input only as a whole token, so "aysel.mammadova" scored 4/4 against inputs "Aysel Mammadova" and "aysel.mammadova@company.az" and passed PASSWORD_MIN_SCORE. Fix: new exported personalWords() lower-cases each input and adds the whole value, the email local part, each domain label of 3+ chars (TLD dropped) and every run of 3+ letters/digits; checkPassword() now calls factory.check(password, personalWords(userInputs)). Because the split sits inside checkPassword, all three callers on main get it without change: server rule passwordProblem() (src/server/auth/password.ts:26, called from src/server/actions/auth.ts:481 with [email, name]), the set-password meter (src/app/(auth)/account/[kind]/[token]/set-password-form.tsx:27) and the Password Forge lab passphraseRules() (inputs userName, email, orgName). The lesson scene meter (src/components/player/scenes.tsx:1600) calls checkPassword(v) with no inputs by design. Regression tests: passwordProblem("aysel.mammadova", [...]) === "weak"; personalWords() split cases incl. Azerbaijani letters; passphraseRules strong=false for a passphrase from the learner's details.
- Evidence: Main: portal/src/lib/password-strength.ts:7-10 `return factory.check(password, userInputs)` passes the inputs unsplit; password.ts:26 calls checkPassword with them; auth.ts:481 passes [row.user.email, row.user.name]. All callers go through checkPassword (grep: set-password-form.tsx:27, scenes.tsx:1600 without inputs, password.ts:26), so the fix in the shared function reaches every one. tests.diff:154-193 adds `personalWords()` (whole value, email local part, domain labels of 3+, every run of 3+ letters/digits, Unicode-aware `/[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/u`) and changes line 9 to `factory.check(password, personalWords(userInputs))`; tests.diff:1871 `passwordProblem("aysel.mammadova", ["Aysel Mammadova", "aysel.mammadova@example.com"])` → "weak", :1882 split expectations, :1898 passphraseRules strong=false. tests/password-domain.test.ts is new on the branch (not on main).
- Smallest fix: Merge the tests branch hunk for portal/src/lib/password-strength.ts and portal/tests/password-domain.test.ts as is.
- Files: portal/src/lib/password-strength.ts, portal/tests/password-domain.test.ts
- Risk: Stricter rule: a passphrase built from the organisation name now fails the Password Forge lab's 'strong' rule and invitation/reset passwords containing the person's own name are refused; existing stored hashes are untouched.

### S-02 · medium · open · effort M
**SSO accounts are linked by email address only**

- Sources: audit:S-02, docs:DOC-8, repo:REP-23
- Detail: [audit:S-02] sso/callback/[tenant]/route.ts L75-L104: the user is found by users.email; the identity provider's iss/sub pair is never stored or compared. When an administrator names a custom emailClaim, the email_verified check is skipped by design. An IdP that lets users change the mapped claim, or a mail alias reassigned to someone else, lets that person sign in as another learner of the same organisation (privileged roles and other organisations are refused). Acknowledged in ADR-033 open items.
  [docs:DOC-8] README roadmap line 291 and ARCHITECTURE.md section 17 line 491 ('The provider's sub is not bound to the account'); API.md line 519 'The person is found by email'. Confirmed: portal/src/app/api/sso/callback/[tenant]/route.ts line 101 selects the user by email alone; the users table (portal/src/server/db/schema.ts lines 161-195) has no subject/issuer column. An IdP that re-issues an address to a different person, or a configured non-standard emailClaim (route.ts line 75, trusted without email_verified), signs the new person into the old account.
  [repo:REP-23] ADR-033 open point: the OIDC callback finds the user by email; binding the IdP subject must be done together with the SSO test (Q14).
- Evidence: portal/src/app/api/sso/callback/[tenant]/route.ts:101 `let [user] = await db().select().from(t.users).where(eq(t.users.email, email))` is the only lookup; :75-77 skip the email_verified check whenever Settings names a custom emailClaim; :114 creates the learner from the email alone; :121-128 opens the session. oidc.ts:143 already checks `claims.iss === p.issuer` and :149 returns every claim, so `claims.sub` is available at route.ts:74 and simply never read. portal/src/server/db/schema.ts:158-204 users has no subject/issuer column. No branch touches route.ts or the users table (demo.diff's schema.ts change is +45 lines of drill tables only, `git diff -w --stat`). tests/sso.test.ts:26-57 covers only token verification and PKCE.
- Smallest fix: schema.ts users (~line 173, next to passwordHash): `ssoSubject: text("sso_subject")`; migration via `npm run db:generate` (drizzle/meta/_journal.json holds only 0000_init; the demo branch adds 0001/0002, so number after it if demo lands first). route.ts inside the try block after line 74: `sub = typeof claims.sub === "string" && claims.sub.length <= 255 ? claims.sub : ""; if (!sub) throw new Error("no_subject")`. After line 105: `if (user.ssoSubject && user.ssoSubject !== sub) return refuse("subject_changed", user.id);` and bind when null: `if (!user.ssoSubject) await db().update(t.users).set({ ssoSubject: sub }).where(eq(t.users.id, user.id))`; include `ssoSubject: sub` in the insert at line 114. Add an 'unlink SSO' path for administrators: clear ssoSubject in the existing reset/status action in people.ts (otherwise a person re-created at the IdP is locked out). Test: a route test with the PGlite helper the tests branch adds (tests/helpers/db.ts) or a pure `subjectDecision(stored, presented)` unit test.
- Files: portal/src/app/api/sso/callback/[tenant]/route.ts, portal/src/server/db/schema.ts, portal/drizzle/<next>_sso_subject.sql, portal/drizzle/meta/_journal.json, portal/src/server/actions/people.ts, portal/messages/{az,en,ru,tr,ro,ka,uk,de,fr,ar}/admin.json (sso refusal reason label, if the audit viewer maps reasons), portal/tests/sso.test.ts
- Risk: Existing SSO users have a null subject and are bound on their next sign-in (no lockout). An organisation that re-provisions a person at its IdP gets 'sso.sign_in_refused subject_changed' until an administrator unlinks. Keeping the emailClaim-without-email_verified behaviour (ADR-033) is unchanged by this fix; the subject binding closes the practical account-swap.
- Depends on: S-09
- Needs the owner: A real IdP test tenant (Entra ID or Google Workspace) to run the end-to-end SSO test (OPEN-QUESTIONS Q14); without it the fix is verified only by unit tests.

### TST-2 · medium · fixed_on_branch (tests) · effort S
**Internationalised domains (.рф .укр .გე .السعودية) could not be proven**

- Sources: tests:TST-2
- Detail: Root cause (diff, portal/src/server/auth/domain-proof.ts): HOST regex demanded a TLD of [a-z]{2,63} and normaliseHost() never converted Unicode, so both пример.рф and example.xn--p1ai returned null and verifyDomainAction/verifyTenantDomainAction refused them. Fix: non-ASCII input that matches UNICODE_HOST (/^[\p{L}\p{N}\p{M}.-]+$/u) is passed through node:url domainToASCII; HOST now also accepts an xn--[a-z0-9-]{1,59} TLD; the ASCII form is what is stored (tenants.domain) and resolved. The guard keeps domainToASCII from turning "example.com/path" into a domain. Callers on main all go through normaliseHost (src/server/actions/settings.ts:120, src/server/actions/platform.ts:98, src/server/mail.ts:117). Regression tests: five IDN cases map to their punycode, ASCII cases unchanged, 12 non-domains still null. Incomplete sibling: see TST-16 (senderDomain regex).
- Evidence: Main: portal/src/server/auth/domain-proof.ts:13 HOST requires a TLD of `[a-z]{2,63}` and :16-19 normaliseHost does no Unicode conversion, so `example.xn--p1ai` and `пример.рф` both return null; every domain entry goes through normaliseHost (settings.ts:120, platform.ts:98, mail.ts:117, grep). tests.diff:194-228 imports domainToASCII from node:url, adds the `xn--[a-z0-9-]{1,59}` TLD alternative and converts only input matching UNICODE_HOST, keeping `example.com/path` from being turned into a domain; tests.diff:1917-1918 assert `example.xn--p1ai` and `пример.рф` → `xn--e1afmkfd.xn--p1ai`. No other branch touches domain-proof.ts.
- Smallest fix: Merge the tests branch hunk for portal/src/server/auth/domain-proof.ts with its tests. The stored form is ASCII (tenants.domain), which is what DNS lookups and the email-domain comparison at route.ts:109 use.

### TST-9 · medium · fixed_on_branch (tests) · effort S
**Device limit could leave one session too many when the app clock runs ahead of the database clock**

- Sources: tests:TST-9
- Detail: Root cause (diff, portal/src/server/auth/session.ts createSession): after inserting the new session it selected all of the user's sessions ordered by lastSeenAt, computed excess = all.length - maxDevices and deleted the first `excess` rows while skipping the new one with `continue`. The new row's lastSeenAt is the database default (DB clock) while the others were stamped by the app server; if the DB clock lags, the new session sorts among the oldest, gets skipped, and one fewer than `excess` is removed, leaving maxDevices + 1 live sessions. Fix: select only the other sessions (ne(sessions.id, id)), excess = others.length + 1 - maxDevices, delete the oldest `excess` of them. Both creators on main go through createSession — password sign-in (src/server/actions/auth.ts:191) and the SSO callback (src/app/api/sso/callback/[tenant]/route.ts:121) — so no sibling is left. Regression tests: LRU eviction with audit 'auth.device_limit'; the clocks-out-of-step case keeps the new session and leaves exactly 2.
- Evidence: Main: portal/src/server/auth/session.ts:35-38 selects every session of the user ordered by lastSeenAt, `excess = all.length - maxDevices`, and `continue`s past the new one without deleting a replacement. The new row's lastSeenAt is the database default (schema.ts:218 `defaultNow()`), the others are stamped by the app server (viewer.ts:79 `set({ lastSeenAt: now })`), so a lagging database clock sorts the new session among the oldest and leaves maxDevices + 1 rows. Both session creators call createSession (auth.ts:191 startSession, route.ts:121 SSO). tests.diff:229-253: `others` = sessions `ne(sessions.id, id)`, `excess = others.length + 1 - maxDevices`, delete the oldest `excess`; tests.diff:2915 'keeps the new session and still enforces the limit ... (clocks out of step)' and :2912 asserts the auth.device_limit audit row.
- Smallest fix: Merge the tests branch hunk for portal/src/server/auth/session.ts and portal/tests/sessions-viewer.test.ts as is.
- Files: portal/src/server/auth/session.ts, portal/tests/sessions-viewer.test.ts
- Risk: None beyond the intended extra deletion: one more audit 'auth.device_limit' row in the out-of-step case.

### DOC-1 · medium · open · effort S
**SSO callback and start ignore the domain proof; learners are auto-created for an unproven saved domain**

- Sources: docs:DOC-1
- Detail: Documented by the docs branch as a known limitation only (ARCHITECTURE.md section 5 line 203 and section 17 line 492; API.md section 9 line 521; cloud-session-reports PR #4 'SSO BUG FOUND (not fixed)'). Confirmed in main: portal/src/app/api/sso/callback/[tenant]/route.ts line 47-50 selects id, slug, domain, plan, features, settings from tenants and never domainVerifiedAt; line 109 admits a new learner when emailDomain(email) === tenant.domain?.toLowerCase() and nothing else, then line 114 inserts the user as active. portal/src/app/api/sso/start/route.ts line 42 gates only on the sso plan feature and settings.identity.ssoEnabled, so the whole flow is reachable by a direct GET /api/sso/start?tenant=slug. The only proof check is on the sign-in page: portal/src/server/auth/sso-routing.ts line 48 refuses SSO when domainVerifiedAt is null, and portal/src/server/actions/auth.ts line 216 selects tenants only where domainVerifiedAt is not null. The proof can be absent while domain is set: portal/src/server/jobs.ts lines 290-297 null domainVerifiedAt after the 7-day grace but keep domain, portal/src/server/actions/platform.ts line 118 lets the operator record a domain with domainVerifiedAt null, and jobs.ts line 286 skips the daily re-check entirely when identity.domainProofForced is set (not mentioned in the docs). Impact is bounded: the tenant's own IdP must still authenticate the person, and route.ts line 103 refuses accounts of other organisations, so no cross-tenant takeover; the broken guarantee is that account creation on a domain is tied to current ownership proof.
- Evidence: Main checkout, confirmed line by line. portal/src/app/api/sso/callback/[tenant]/route.ts:47-50 selects id, slug, domain, plan, features, settings and NOT domainVerifiedAt; :99 gates only on settings.identity.ssoEnabled + the 'sso' plan feature; :106-109 autoCreate branch compares emailDomain(email) !== tenant.domain?.toLowerCase() only; :114 inserts the learner with status 'active', activatedAt now. portal/src/app/api/sso/start/route.ts:33 selects slug, plan, features, settings (no domain, no domainVerifiedAt); :42 gates only on the 'sso' feature and (!test && !ssoEnabled), so GET /api/sso/start?tenant=<slug> starts the flow for an unproven domain. The proof is checked only on the sign-in page: portal/src/server/auth/sso-routing.ts:48 returns the password step when !tenant.domainVerifiedAt; portal/src/server/actions/auth.ts:213-217 selects tenants where isNotNull(domainVerifiedAt). Domain-set-but-unproven is a real state: portal/src/server/jobs.ts:290 computes `removed` after DOMAIN_PROOF_GRACE_DAYS and :297 `.set({ settings: patched, ...(removed ? { domainVerifiedAt: null } : {}) })` nulls the proof and keeps `domain`; portal/src/server/actions/platform.ts:118 `.set({ domain: host, domainVerifiedAt: verified ? now : null, settings })` records a domain with a null proof when the TXT record is not found and force is off. jobs.ts:286 `if (!tenant.domain || identity.domainProofForced || now - last < DAY) continue;` does skip the re-check when forced, but in that case platform.ts:103/114/118 has already set domainVerifiedAt (verified = found || force), so forced proof is an operator override by design, not part of this defect. Branches: grep -n 'domainVerifiedAt|domain_unproven|domainProofForced' over audit/security/tests/docs/demo .diff hits only demo.diff:2191 (seed) and demo.diff:3688-4760 (schema moved, unchanged); no diff has a hunk for portal/src/app/api/sso/**. docs.diff:865, :1094 and :1383 document it as a known limitation (ARCHITECTURE.md sections 5 and 17); cloud-session-reports.md:17 says 'SSO BUG FOUND (not fixed)'. Impact is bounded as the finding says: route.ts:103 refuses accounts of other organisations and :104 privileged roles; the IdP still authenticates the person.
- Smallest fix: Two selects and two guards, mirroring sso-routing.ts:48. (1) portal/src/app/api/sso/start/route.ts:33 add `domainVerifiedAt: t.tenants.domainVerifiedAt` to the select, and at :42 change the gate to `if (!featuresFor(...).has("sso") || (!test && (!tenant.settings.identity.ssoEnabled || !tenant.domainVerifiedAt))) redirect(failed);` so the administrator's &test=1 check still works before the proof lands, as ssoEnabled already is exempt there. (2) portal/src/app/api/sso/callback/[tenant]/route.ts:48 add `domainVerifiedAt: t.tenants.domainVerifiedAt` to the select and, right after the `sso_off` refuse at :99 (after the state.test early return at :88-92, so the settings test is unaffected), add `if (!tenant.domainVerifiedAt) return refuse("domain_unproven");`. Put it before the user lookup rather than inside the autoCreate branch: the sign-in page already refuses SSO for every address on an unproven domain, so refusing the whole callback is the consistent rule and also covers the invited->active activation at :116-118. `refuse` writes the reason into the sso.sign_in_refused audit meta and redirects to /sign-in?error=sso, so no new message keys are needed. ### MIS-1 · medium · not_an_issue · effort M
**IDN tenant domain is stored in ASCII but every e-mail-domain comparison uses the raw Unicode domain (sibling of TST-2)**

- Sources: MIS-1
- Detail: The tests branch makes normaliseHost() return domainToASCII() for internationalised names (portal/src/server/auth/domain-proof.ts, new HOST/UNICODE_HOST), so a proven tenant domain such as пример.рф is stored as xn--e1afmkfd.xn--p1ai. On main, emailDomain() (portal/src/server/auth/sso-routing.ts:27-31) only lower-cases the part after '@' and is compared with tenant.domain as a plain string: SSO callback refuses the person as foreign_domain (portal/src/app/api/sso/callback/[tenant]/route.ts:109), SSO routing falls back to password (sso-routing.ts:46-48), sign-in routing (portal/src/server/actions/auth.ts:211), and the cross-tenant foreign-domain guard in people add/import never matches (portal/src/server/actions/people.ts:123 and :528), so another tenant can add people under a proven IDN domain. mail.ts:117 compares normaliseHost(senderDomain) with tenant.domain and is the only consistent site. TST-16 (senderDomain regex) is a different sibling.
- Evidence: The comparison mismatch is unreachable. Every e-mail entry point validates with zod 4.6.7 z.email() (portal/package.json:44), whose default pattern (portal/node_modules/zod/v4/core/regexes.js:34, applied at schemas.js:207) is ASCII-only with a `[A-Za-z]{2,}$` top-level label: sign-in auth.ts:203/:250/:267/:436, SSO callback route.ts:20/:79 (an IdP claim user@пример.рф fails as no_email_claim before :109), people add people.ts:58, import people.ts:525, operator tenant creation platform.ts:35. So emailDomain() (sso-routing.ts:27-31) never sees a Unicode domain, and a punycode IDN TLD (xn--p1ai) is refused too. For an IDN label under an ASCII TLD (пример.com → xn--e1afmkfd.com, which main's HOST regex at domain-proof.ts:13 already accepts in punycode) the only enterable form is user@xn--e1afmkfd.com, which emailDomain returns as-is and which equals the stored value, so the foreign-domain guards at people.ts:123/:528 and the SSO checks hold. No branch touches emailDomain (grep of all five diffs). Real residual, different finding: on the tests branch a tenant can prove пример.рф (normaliseHost → xn--e1afmkfd.xn--p1ai, tests.diff domain-proof.ts hunk) but nobody with an address on that domain can be added, imported or signed in, because z.email() refuses both forms.
- Smallest fix: Nothing for the stated bug. If IDN e-mail addresses are to be supported: (1) pass a pattern to every z.email() that accepts punycode labels (`xn--` TLD), and (2) make emailDomain() return domainToASCII(part after '@') with normaliseHost's guard so the stored ASCII form matches; add one case to tests/password-domain.test.ts and the SSO routing test. Without (1), (2) is dead code.
- Files: portal/src/server/auth/sso-routing.ts, portal/src/server/actions/auth.ts, portal/src/server/actions/people.ts, portal/src/app/api/sso/callback/[tenant]/route.ts, portal/src/server/actions/platform.ts, portal/tests/password-domain.test.ts
- Risk: Relaxing z.email() widens what reaches mail sending and SSO; must keep the domainToASCII guard so 'a/b' or query strings cannot become a domain.

**Warm-up script inserts a 2FA-verified admin session straight into the DB and never removes it**

- Sources: demo:DMO-10
- Detail: scripts/demo-session.ts (diff lines 1963-2002) selects admin@<DEMO_DOMAIN>, inserts a t.sessions row with twoFactorVerified: true, expiresAt +20 min, userAgent 'demo warm-up', and prints the raw token to stdout for demo.mjs to send as the cy_session/__Host-cy_session cookie. It refuses when DATABASE_URL is set (local embedded DB only). The row is not deleted after warm-up, so for 20 minutes it appears in the admin's device list and counts toward the tenant's maxDevices limit (session.ts revokes the excess on sign-in). The warm-up hits /admin, /admin/campaigns, /admin/threats, /admin/leadership and the drill pages with an admin session, which also runs advanceDrill for the zero UUID (harmless 404).

'__Host-cy_session' : 'cy_session'}=${token}` (matches portal/src/server/auth/session.ts:13) to /sign-in, /admin/drill, /admin/drill/<zero>, /api/admin/drill/<zero>, /admin, /admin/campaigns, /admin/campaigns/<zero>, /admin/threats, /admin/leadership. `grep -n sessions demo.diff` shows only the insert at :1992 and the schema move; no delete anywhere, so 'never removes it' is correct. Two impact sub-claims are REFUTED on main: (a) there is no device list: `grep -rn t.sessions portal/src/server/actions` hits only profile.ts:45 and auth.ts:325 (set twoFactorVerified) and people.ts:325 (delete all sessions on status change); no component lists sessions; the only 'devices' message key (portal/messages/en/common.json:129) is a training category (portal/src/lib/domain/catalog.ts:3). (b) the device limit: session.ts:34-41 does revoke the excess on sign-in, but the demo seed sets no maxDevices (grep on portal/scripts/seed.ts and seed-data.ts: no hits) and the default is null (portal/src/lib/tenant-defaults.ts:231), so it only matters if the presenter sets a limit within the 20 minutes. After 20 minutes the row is dead: portal/src/server/auth/viewer.ts:68 refuses an expired session and portal/src/server/jobs.ts:361 purges expired rows (JOBS_ENABLED=1 is set by demo.mjs in --prod mode, demo.diff:2150). The drill GET is a poll, not a mutation: demo.diff:2422-2441 /api/admin/drill/[id] GET calls advanceDrill then drillView and returns 404 for the zero UUID (run is null), harmless as the finding says. The suggested fix is NOT implementable as written: the server process holds the embedded PGlite database (CLAUDE.md: single-process; demo.mjs's own port check at demo.diff:2085-2089 says only one process may open .data/pg), so a second `tsx scripts/demo-session.ts --revoke` cannot run while the server is up, and sign-out exists only as a server action (portal/src/server/actions/auth.ts:496 signOutAction; no HTTP route under portal/src/app/api for it), which a plain fetch cannot call without the Next-Action id.

Do not shorten the TTL: in development each of the nine warm-up pages compiles on first request with a 300 s budget each (demo.diff:2167-2171), so a shorter expiry can cut the warm-up off. Keep the DATABASE_URL refusal. If the owner wants the row gone immediately after warm-up, the smallest working change is a POST /api/auth/sign-out route (apiViewer -> invalidateSession(v.sessionId) from session.ts:76 -> clearSessionCookie) called by demo.mjs as the last warm-up request; that is a new public endpoint and belongs with the security branch's review, not in the demo script.

### TST-7 · medium · fixed_on_branch (tests) · effort S
**A simulation link opened twice at the same moment recorded two clicks (two risks, two events)**

- Sources: tests:TST-7
- Detail: Root cause (diff, campaigns.ts recordClick): the guard was an in-memory check (if (!row.r.clickedAt && !cancelled)) followed by an unconditional UPDATE, so two concurrent requests (double tap, link preview + click, link + QR) each inserted a 'phishing_click' behavior_risk, emitted a 'phishing.clicked' webhook event and recomputed the score, counting twice against the person. Fix: the UPDATE now carries WHERE clickedAt IS NULL and RETURNING, openedAt is set with coalesce(openedAt, now) in SQL, and only the claimant inserts the risk/event. recordOpen() on main already uses the same conditional form (isNull(openedAt)), and threats.ts:91 sets reportedAt with isNull(), so the tracking family is now consistent. Regression tests: sequential second click leaves one risk; Promise.all(link, qr) leaves one risk and one event.
- Evidence: Main: portal/src/server/services/campaigns.ts:139 in-memory guard `if (!row.r.clickedAt && !cancelled)`, :141 unconditional update, :143-154 behaviorRisks insert, emitEvent and recomputeRisk inside that guard, so two concurrent requests both pass :139. recordOpen :110-121 already uses isNull(openedAt) and threats.ts:91 sets reportedAt with isNull(). tests.diff 301-327: the update carries isNull(clickedAt) and .returning(), openedAt = coalesce(openedAt, now) in SQL, and the risk/event/recompute run only for the claimant. Tests: 'records a click once when the link is opened twice at the same time' (Promise.all link + qr → 1 risk, 1 event) and the sequential second click in 'records a click once…'.
- Smallest fix: Merge the tests branch as is.
- Files: portal/src/server/services/campaigns.ts, portal/tests/campaign-flows.test.ts
- Risk: None; the demo branch's drill calls recordClick(db, token, "link") with the same signature.

### DMO-4 · medium · open · effort S

Branch: demo.diff only touches sendQueuedSms (campaigns.ts hunk @@ -269: notExists drillRuns) and queues no lure; DEMO.md Safety says 'A drill never sends anything' and ADR-034 §3/§6 say 'Heç bir məktub və SMS göndərilmir'. ### DMO-5 · medium · partial (demo) · effort S
**No timer and a 20 s lease: a drill freezes when nobody polls, and a crash replays one step whose safety depends on the tests branch**

- Sources: demo:DMO-5
- Detail: services/drill.ts applies due events only inside advanceDrill, called by the polled route and by the page render ('There is no timer', diff line 5747). If the presenter closes the tab, the drill stays 'running' with unsent recipients and the campaign stays status 'running' until someone opens /admin/drill/[id]; history shows it as Live. LEASE_MS = 20_000 (line 5778): a server dying mid-apply leaves lease_until up to 20 s ahead, so the dashboard shows no progress for up to 20 s, then another poll takes over; applied_until is CAS-updated after each step, so exactly the step in flight is replayed. Replay safety per kind: deliver (isNull sentAt guard), click (recordClick checks clickedAt on main), report (reportedAt check added, tested at diff 6475-6490) are idempotent; 'train' is not on main: completeLesson awards XP again and attestModule issues a second certificate on repeat, bugs fixed only on the tests branch (PR #3: 'double XP on repeated completion', 'duplicate certificates on repeated attestation'). One failed step is logged and skipped (line 5976-5979) rather than surfaced to the presenter.
- Evidence: Confirmed on the demo branch (demo.diff drill.ts hunk): header comment 'There is no timer: whoever polls the drill ... applies the events that are due'; advanceDrill is called only from portal/src/app/api/admin/drill/[id]/route.ts GET and portal/src/app/(admin)/admin/drill/[id]/page.tsx; `const LEASE_MS = 20_000`; lease claim `where appliedUntil = applied and (leaseUntil is null or leaseUntil < now)`; per-step CAS `set appliedUntil: applied+1 where appliedUntil = applied`; failed step swallowed with console.error (hunk lines 5976-5979) and never shown in the feed; finishDrill only runs inside advanceDrill. demo.diff does not touch portal/src/server/jobs.ts (not in its file list), so no background tick advances drills; drillHistory reports `finished: !!run.finishedAt`, and main campaigns.ts:237-240 campaignTick completes the campaign after 14 days while drill_runs.finishedAt stays null, so an abandoned drill shows as live until someone opens it. Replay-safety correction: the finding overstates the 'train' hazard. On main, progress.ts:66-71 completeLesson sets xp = 0 when lessonProgress.completedAt is already set, and progress.ts:212-216 attestModule returns null unless moduleProgress.status is 'awaiting_attestation' (it is 'completed' after the first attestation, :218-221), so a SEQUENTIAL replay of 'train' (the crash case: the dead request cannot race) awards no second XP, stores no second attestation and issues no second certificate; only attempts and secondsSpent grow (progress.ts:83-84). The tests branch bug ('double XP', 'duplicate certificates', tests.diff progress.ts hunks) is the CONCURRENT read-then-write race, which here needs a still-alive request to stall more than 20 s inside one step while another poll takes over. So the demo branch is safe on main for the realistic crash, and the tests branch closes the stall overlap.
- Smallest fix: In portal/src/server/jobs.ts add one step after `campaigns` (line 54): `await step("drills", async () => { const open = await db.select({ id: t.drillRuns.id, tenantId: t.drillRuns.tenantId }).from(t.drillRuns).where(isNull(t.drillRuns.finishedAt)); for (const d of open) await advanceDrill(db, d.tenantId, d.id, now); return open.length; })` importing advanceDrill from ./services/drill; advanceDrill is already lease-safe and finishes the drill and its campaign itself, so an abandoned drill completes within a minute. Add a replay test for 'train' next to 'does not report twice' in portal/tests/drill-service.test.ts (reset appliedUntil to the first train event, advance, assert certificates and xpEvents counts unchanged). Skip surfacing failed steps to the presenter.
- Files: portal/src/server/jobs.ts, portal/tests/drill-service.test.ts, portal/tests/jobs-runner.test.ts
- Risk: The jobs tick now imports services/drill.ts; a drill whose step throws every time would be retried once a minute (each retry logs and skips, so no loop). The tests branch's conditional-claim rewrite of completeLesson/attestModule and the demo branch's drill both touch progress.ts callers: merge order does not matter for correctness, but run tests/drill-service.test.ts after both land.
- Depends on: DMO-18
- Needs the owner: Nothing.

### MIS-4 · low · open · effort S
**Drill poll is a state-changing GET with no Origin check, contradicting the security review's CSRF claim and API.md's own convention**

- Sources: MIS-4
- Detail: GET /api/admin/drill/[id] (portal/src/app/api/admin/drill/[id]/route.ts:17-25) calls advanceDrill(), which writes recipients, risks, threat reports, lesson progress, attestations and certificates. apiViewer() (portal/src/server/auth/api.ts:12-20) checks session, 2FA and permission only; the Origin check exists for POST handlers alone. docs/SECURITY_REVIEW.md ('What was checked and found sound' → CSRF: 'state-changing work is never done on GET') and docs/API.md:297 ('A GET … returns 405, because creating links changes data') both state the invariant the drill breaks. With SameSite=Lax cookies a cross-site top-level link can advance an admin's running drill; impact is small (only already-due synthetic events) but the documented invariant is false after merge. DMO-6 covers only the polling cost.
- Evidence: demo worktree portal/src/app/api/admin/drill/[id]/route.ts:11-19: `GET` → apiViewer('campaigns.write') → `advanceDrill(db(), v.tenant.id, id)` → drillView. main portal/src/server/auth/api.ts:12-20 apiViewer checks session, 2FA gap and permission only. demo services/drill.ts:205 advanceDrill applies due events via recordOpen/recordClick/recordSubmit (:153-160), submitThreatReport (:167), completeLesson + attestModule (:179-181), recomputeRisk (:174/:183) and updates drill_runs lease/applied_until/risk_trail (:221-262). main request.ts:79 sameOrigin is used only by POST handlers (people/[kind]/route.ts:69, subtitles/route.ts:33, tutor/route.ts:23) and returns true when Origin is absent (:70), so it would not protect a GET navigation; proxy.ts has no origin/sec-fetch logic; session cookie sameSite 'lax' (session.ts:60), so a cross-site top-level link carries it. security worktree docs/SECURITY_REVIEW.md:213 'state-changing work is never done on GET'; docs worktree docs/API.md:297 'A GET … returns 405, because creating links changes data'. Callers: live-drill.tsx:73 and :119 (fetch GET); skipDrillAction (actions/drill.ts:49) is a server action and already origin-checked by Next. Impact: only already-due synthetic events of the admin's own running drill; no attacker input beyond the id.
- Smallest fix: In route.ts: rename the current handler to `POST`, add `if (!sameOrigin(request)) return new Response('Forbidden', { status: 403 })` after apiViewer; add a read-only `GET` that returns `drillView(db(), await drillById(db(), v.tenant.id, id), locale)` (drillById exists, services/drill.ts:407). In live-drill.tsx change the two `fetch(\`/api/admin/drill/${view.id}\`, …)` calls to `method: 'POST'`. Then both documents stay true. tests/drill-service.test.ts exercises the service, not the route, so no test changes.
- Files: portal/src/app/api/admin/drill/[id]/route.ts, portal/src/components/admin/drill/live-drill.tsx, docs/API.md
- Risk: Any other poller of the GET would stop advancing the drill; only live-drill.tsx calls it. Behind a proxy the POST needs TRUST_PROXY set correctly for sameOrigin, as the other POST handlers already do.

**Flakiness risks: 23 PGlite boots per run, no per-test timeout, time-dependent and order-coupled tests**

- Sources: tests:TST-22

Multi-step tests with no explicit timeout: learning-actions.test.ts:49 'walks a module lesson by lesson', secops-flows.test.ts:107-113 seven sequential submitThreatReport, password-domain.test.ts:24-33 three Argon2id hashes (m=19456,t=2). Skip fake timers: the only midnight-sensitive assertion is already guarded, and freezing Date while PGlite's now() keeps running would break more than it fixes. Skip migrating the 14 older files onto helpers/db.ts (refactor, not a flake fix). Add `maxWorkers` only if the first Actions run is red or OOMs.

### TST-19 · low · open · effort S
**Every pull request from an in-repo branch runs the whole workflow twice**

- Sources: tests:TST-19
- Detail: ci.yml triggers on push to branches: ["**"] and on pull_request. A PR opened from a branch in the same repository fires both events; the concurrency group is keyed on github.ref (refs/heads/<branch> vs refs/pull/N/merge), so the two runs do not cancel each other. Both jobs (checks ~10-15 min, build up to the 30 min cap) run twice per push, doubling minutes and giving two status checks to pick from when marking required checks.
- Evidence: tests branch .github/workflows/ci.yml:3-6 'on: push: branches: ["**"]' plus 'pull_request:'; :9-11 'concurrency: group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}'. For a PR from an in-repo branch the push run has ref refs/heads/<branch> and the PR run refs/pull/<n>/merge, so they are different groups and both run both jobs (checks :27-56, build :58-78, each timeout-minutes: 30). No workflow_dispatch trigger. The security branch's security.yml:4-11 already uses the push-main + pull_request + workflow_dispatch form, so the two workflows disagree.
- Smallest fix: In ci.yml replace lines 3-6 with: on: push: branches: [main]; pull_request:; workflow_dispatch: (the same shape as security.yml:4-11). Nothing else changes; the concurrency group then has one run per PR plus one per push to main.
- Files: .github/workflows/ci.yml
- Risk: A branch without a PR gets no CI run (open a draft PR or use workflow_dispatch); required-check names stay the same.
- Depends on: T-01
- Needs the owner: 

### TST-21 · low · open · effort S
**Build job has no Next.js build cache and no dependency on the checks job**

- Sources: tests:TST-21
- Detail: The build job repeats npm ci (cached via setup-node) but never caches portal/.next/cache, so `next build --webpack` compiles the 139 MB standalone output from scratch every run; with 106 lessons × 10 locales and a 30-minute timeout this is the step most likely to hit the cap on a slow runner. The two jobs run in parallel with no `needs`, which is fine for speed but means a red lint still spends build minutes. The `postbuild` check (scripts/check-build.mjs) runs correctly through `npm run build`.
- Evidence: tests branch only (main has no .github/: `ls ../.github` fails). wt/tests/.github/workflows/ci.yml:58-78 build job = checkout, setup-node (cache: npm, portal/package-lock.json), npm ci, `npm run build`; no actions/cache step for portal/.next/cache and no `needs:` (jobs section lines 26-78, both jobs top-level). `next build --webpack` does write a persistent cache: portal/.next/cache/{webpack,swc,fetch-cache} exists locally (612 MB incl. dev fetch-cache). portal/package.json:7-8 build + postbuild (check-build.mjs) run as claimed; scripts/check-build.mjs:16-40 walks .next/server/app and exits 1 on the fallback host. No other diff (audit/security/docs/demo) touches ci.yml. Adjacent and larger minute-sink: ci.yml:3-6 `push: branches: ["**"]` plus `pull_request` runs both jobs twice for every same-repo PR (security.yml on the security branch uses `push: branches: [main]`).
- Smallest fix: In .github/workflows/ci.yml build job, after the setup-node step add:
        - uses: actions/cache@v4
          with:
            path: portal/.next/cache
            key: nextjs-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('portal/package-lock.json') }}-${{ hashFiles('portal/src/**', 'portal/messages/**', 'portal/next.config.*') }}
            restore-keys: nextjs-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('portal/package-lock.json') }}-
  (hashFiles paths are workspace-relative; defaults.run.working-directory does not apply). Also change line 5 to `branches: [main]` so PR pushes run once. Skip `needs: checks`: it serialises the two jobs and roughly doubles wall-clock for a red-lint saving the owner has not asked for.
- Files: .github/workflows/ci.yml
- Risk: None to code. A stale webpack cache is self-validated by next build. Cache save/restore of a few hundred MB costs ~30-60 s per run; net gain unmeasured until one Actions run with and without it.

### MIS-5 · low · open · effort S
**Demo compose secrets will probably trip the security branch's gitleaks scan**

- Sources: MIS-5
- Detail: portal/docker-compose.demo.yml (demo branch) commits APP_SECRET: demo-only-not-secret-0123456789abcdef0123456789 (line 17; Shannon entropy 4.52 bits, above the 3.5 threshold of gitleaks' generic-api-key rule and matching its 'secret … :' pattern), POSTGRES_PASSWORD (line 24) and a password in DATABASE_URL (line 13). .gitleaks.toml on the security branch allowlists only test-only-app-secret, dev-only-secret-change-me and the seed password, and security.yml scans the whole history (--all) on every push to main and weekly, so the first run after merging demo likely fails. SEC-3 notes false positives in general; this is the concrete one the merge creates. Not executed here (plausible).

Measured Shannon entropy: line 17 value 4.517 bits (47 chars) > 3.5 threshold of generic-api-key, keyword SECRET + ':' separator match; line 24 value 3.409 < 3.5, so it should not trip the entropy gate; line 13 'secret' is followed by '@', which the generic-api-key regex does not accept as a separator, so it is unlikely to match. Not executed: gitleaks was never run (cloud-session-reports.md PR #2 'Not verified'), and its default stopword list (which may contain 'demo') could not be checked offline. Note: with fetch-depth 0 and --all the first run also scans origin's unmerged branches, so the demo branch is scanned as soon as both are on origin, merge or not.
- Smallest fix: Add one unanchored line '''demo-only-not-secret''' to the regexes array in .gitleaks.toml (regexTarget secret, lines 12-19) with a comment pointing at portal/docker-compose.demo.yml; harmless if the scanner would have passed anyway. Confirm on the first Security workflow run.
- Files: .gitleaks.toml

### MIS-12 · low · open · effort S
**PGlite-from-journal tests cannot catch the regenerated-0000 upgrade failure that D-01 warns about**

- Sources: MIS-12
- Detail: tests/helpers/db.ts (tests branch) and tests/drill-service.test.ts (demo branch) both build a fresh PGlite and run migrate() over drizzle/meta/_journal.json, and ci.yml runs only these. A regenerated 0000_init.sql with a new `when` (the convention ARCHITECTURE.md:210 documents) migrates a fresh database fine, so CI stays green while an existing database (the :3100 presentation copy, the Docker demo volume, any customer) would re-run CREATE TABLE and crash on start — the D-01/DMO-1 failure. Nothing in either CI workflow asserts that the journal only grows.
- Evidence: tests worktree portal/tests/helpers/db.ts:18-23 and demo worktree portal/tests/drill-service.test.ts:15-24 both `new PGlite()` + `migrate(..., { migrationsFolder: drizzle })`; ci.yml:53-54 runs only vitest. Main has 16 more tests doing the same (grep migrationsFolder), none reads _journal.json (grep of main, tests and demo test folders: no hit). Migrator rule in node_modules/drizzle-orm/pg-core/dialect.js:57-67: applies every entry whose folderMillis is greater than the last `created_at` in __drizzle_migrations, so a regenerated 0000_init with a newer `when` re-runs its CREATE TABLEs on an existing database, and a changed 0000 with the same `when` is silently skipped (drift). The container runs node scripts/migrate.mjs at every start (portal/scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh:18-19, Dockerfile:50), so that is the crash loop. Main and demo journals both keep idx 0 tag 0000_init when 1793051964708; demo adds idx 1-2 without touching 0000_init.sql (demo stat). docs branch ARCHITECTURE.md:210 and README.md:272 still document regeneration; ROADMAP.md:69 item 1.5 asks for 'CI proves an upgrade from the previous release's schema'.
- Smallest fix: New portal/tests/migrations-journal.test.ts (no database): read drizzle/meta/_journal.json and assert entries[0] equals {idx 0, tag '0000_init', when 1793051964708}, idx is sequential, `when` strictly increases, every tag has drizzle/<tag>.sql, and sha256 of drizzle/0000_init.sql equals a pinned constant (catches a regenerated or edited baseline whether or not `when` changed). The full upgrade test (apply a tagged previous release's drizzle folder, then the current one) is ROADMAP 1.5 and waits for a first release tag.
- Files: portal/tests/migrations-journal.test.ts
- Risk: The test fails on purpose when anyone regenerates 0000_init, which the docs branch still describes as the convention; the constant must be changed deliberately with a migration review.
- Depends on: 
- Needs the owner: Confirm that 0000_init.sql is frozen from now on (ADR-034 point 5 and ROADMAP 1.5 say so; docs branch README.md:272 and ARCHITECTURE.md:210 say the opposite).

### D-01 · high · partial (demo) · effort S
**The migration history is regenerated from scratch**

- Sources: audit:D-01, docs:DOC-5, repo:REP-48
- Detail: [audit:D-01] portal/drizzle holds one migration; README says 'Until the first release there is one migration' (ADR-019); every schema change so far deleted and regenerated 0000_init.sql and required db:reset. docker-entrypoint.sh applies migrations on every start; a regenerated init carries a newer timestamp, so on an existing database it would be re-applied, fail on existing tables and leave the container in a restart loop. Migrations have never been applied to a real PostgreSQL in tests (only PGlite). Harmless today, a production outage the first time the habit continues after a customer goes live.
  [docs:DOC-5] ARCHITECTURE.md section 6 line 210: 'created by one migration, drizzle/0000_init.sql. Until the first release that migration is regenerated instead of adding new ones'; README line 272 repeats it. Confirmed: portal/drizzle contains only 0000_init.sql and meta. The docs present this as a convention; the audit rates it High because any instance already migrated (demo copy on :3100, Docker stacks) will fail or diverge on the next schema change, and the entrypoint applies pending migrations on start (ARCHITECTURE.md section 16).
  [repo:REP-48] README 'Until the first release there is one migration': schema changes rebuild drizzle/0000_init.sql (rm -rf drizzle && drizzle-kit generate --name init) and a database created from the previous init cannot be upgraded by db:migrate (it would rerun the whole init and fail on existing tables). The audit branch rates this High: once anything is deployed, the next schema change crashes the container at start.
- Evidence: Main: portal/drizzle holds only 0000_init.sql + meta (ls); portal/drizzle/meta/_journal.json has one entry, when=1793051964708. `git log --follow drizzle/0000_init.sql` shows three commits (3c2367d, 851d4fa, a7990d3) and the journal `when` changed each time (1792346508116 -> 1792529172176 -> 1793051964708); `git diff --stat 851d4fa a7990d3 -- drizzle` shows 0000_init.sql edited in place (+12 lines) instead of a 0001 file. drizzle-orm/pg-core/dialect.js:57-67 applies a migration whenever the last applied row's created_at < journal `when`, so an existing database created from an older init re-runs the whole init and fails on CREATE TABLE. portal/scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh:7,18-19 runs `node scripts/migrate.mjs` under `set -eu` on every start, so that failure is a restart loop. portal/README.md:308 still instructs `rm -rf drizzle && npx drizzle-kit generate --name init`. Tests only migrate PGlite (portal/tests/*.test.ts migrate(drizzle(pglite)...), e.g. auth-security.test.ts:74); main has no .github at all. Branch demo: `git -C wt/demo ls-files portal/drizzle` tracks 0001_live_drill.sql, 0002_drill_risk_trail.sql, meta/0001_snapshot.json, meta/0002_snapshot.json and a 3-entry _journal.json whose entry 0 keeps when=1793051964708 (0000 unchanged); DECISIONS.md ADR-034 item 5 in demo.diff:195 states 0000 was not regenerated and pushed migrations are never edited. Demo's portal/README.md hunks (demo.diff lines 1954-1958, README hunks at @@ -13, -88, -329) do not touch README:308. Branch docs: docs.diff:1101 (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6) repeats 'Until the first release that migration is regenerated'. Branch tests: .github/workflows/ci.yml (tests.diff) runs vitest on PGlite via tests/helpers/db.ts:21 migrate(drizzle(pglite)); no PostgreSQL service, no migrate.mjs run.
- Smallest fix: (1) portal/README.md:307-308: delete the 'Until the first release there is one migration' bullet and write 'drizzle/0000_init.sql is frozen (2026-11-05); every schema change adds the next file with `npm run db:generate`; a committed migration is never edited'; same one sentence replaces docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6 line 'Until the first release...' on the docs branch, and docs/build/DECISIONS.md gets a one-line ADR pointing at ADR-034 item 5 (already written on the demo branch). (2) Guard test portal/tests/migrations-frozen.test.ts: read drizzle/meta/_journal.json and assert entries[0].tag==='0000_init' and entries[0].when===1793051964708 and sha256(0000_init.sql) equals the pinned hash, with a message 'add 000N, never regenerate'. (3) .github/workflows/ci.yml (tests branch): add a job `migrations-postgres` with `services: postgres: image: postgres:16-alpine` and run `DATABASE_URL=postgres://... node scripts/migrate.mjs` twice; the second run must print 'Migrations applied' with nothing to do (idempotence on real PostgreSQL). The upgrade-from-previous-release test waits until the first tag exists.
- Files: portal/README.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/build/DECISIONS.md, portal/tests/migrations-frozen.test.ts, .github/workflows/ci.yml
- Risk: None to data. Migration numbering: the demo branch owns 0001 and 0002, so any other branch adding a migration (MASTER-PLAN 1.3 lesson_attempts) must be generated after demo lands and become 0003; two branches each creating 0001 would collide in the journal. The :3100 presentation copy and local PGlite databases created from main's 0000 upgrade cleanly with db:migrate once demo lands (0000's `when` unchanged).

### DMO-1 · high · needs_owner_decision (demo) · effort S
**Incremental migrations 0001/0002 vs repo convention of regenerating 0000_init.sql: incremental must win**

- Sources: demo:DMO-1
- Detail: Branch adds portal/drizzle/0001_live_drill.sql (drill_runs table, 2 FKs, index) and 0002_drill_risk_trail.sql (risk_trail jsonb column), plus meta/_journal.json entries idx 1 (when 1793858324572) and idx 2 (when 1793861172751) and two 6,000-line snapshots (these three meta files are committed on the branch but missing from demo.diff). Main's drizzle/ has only 0000_init.sql + 0000_snapshot.json, and git log shows every schema change so far (851d4fa, a7990d3) rewrote 0000_init.sql in place; the owner's memory rule says 'regenerate drizzle/0000_init.sql from scratch, migrate, reseed'. scripts/migrate.ts and migrate.mjs use drizzle's migrator, which replays the journal and applies entries newer than the last applied tag, so existing local DBs (dev :3000, presentation :3100) that ran 0000 will pick up 0001+0002 via db:migrate, whereas a regenerated 0000 would have crashed any already-migrated server (audit High finding). ADR-034 §5 (DECISIONS.md diff line 195) declares the new rule: a pushed migration is never edited, a new column is a new migration. 0002 exists only because risk_trail was added in a later commit of the same unreleased branch.

ADR-034 §5 (demo.diff L195, docs/build/DECISIONS.md) states the new rule. Contradictions that survive the merge: main portal/README.md:308 ('Until the first release there is one migration ... regenerate drizzle/0000_init.sql'), DECISIONS.md ADR-019 result (L87), the owner's memory rule, and on the docs branch README (docs.diff L279 'single initial migration, regenerated until then') and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (docs.diff L1101 '51 tables, created by one migration'). EOL note: schema.ts is CRLF on main (`git ls-files --eol`: i/crlf) and LF on the demo branch (i/lf), so the 2109-line schema.ts hunk is 45 real lines (`git diff -w --stat`); no other branch touches schema.ts or drizzle/ (file lists of the other four diffs), so no conflict, but the merge flips that file's line endings. The :3100 presentation copy is a separate checkout (scratchpad/demo/portal with its own .data, launch-demo.mjs L1-8), not the repo's .data/pg.
- Smallest fix: Adopt incremental (the only non-destructive option given the migrator semantics): merge the demo branch as is; rewrite portal/README.md:308 to 'Every schema change is a new migration: `npm run db:generate` writes the next index; a pushed migration is never edited' (drop the regenerate sentence); same one-sentence fix in docs.diff's README L279 and ARCHITECTURE.md L1101 ('52 tables, three migrations'); add the rule to CLAUDE.md (one bullet) and replace the memory line 'regenerate drizzle/0000_init.sql from scratch' in cylosof-rebuild-project.md L21. Then stop the :3000 dev server and run `npm --prefix portal run db:migrate` (not db:reset). The :3100 copy needs nothing unless the owner wants the drill there (then rebuild that copy and migrate its own .data).
- Files: portal/README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/build/DECISIONS.md, README.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/cylosof-rebuild-project.md
- Risk: A local .data/pg created from an older regenerated 0000 (different `when`) fails db:migrate with 'already exists' and needs db:reset (README:308 already documents this). **Development fallback APP_SECRET is public: rotate stored secrets if any local or demo database ever held real ones**

### S-07 · medium · open · effort M
**One application secret, no key versioning or rotation**

- Sources: audit:S-07
- Detail: crypto.ts L8-L17, domain-proof.ts L22-L24, totp.ts L42-L44: APP_SECRET derives the AES-GCM key for every stored secret (SMTP, SSO, LDAP, webhook, TOTP), the backup-code HMAC and each tenant's DNS proof value. Ciphertexts carry a v1 prefix but no key id. A leaked secret cannot be rotated without re-entering every integration secret, re-enrolling every authenticator and re-publishing every customer's DNS TXT record (proofs lapse after 7 days); losing it is a data-loss event (README 'APP_SECRET is data').
- Evidence: portal/src/server/crypto.ts:8-17: one secret, key(purpose)=sha256(purpose:secret); encryptSecret (:19-24) emits 'v1:iv:tag:data' with no key id; decryptSecret (:26-37) accepts v1 only with the single current key. Consumers of that one key: tenants.settings identity.sso.clientSecretEnc, identity.ldap.passwordEnc, email.passwordEnc, integrations.webhookSecretEnc (actions/settings.ts:245,254,312,483; read in api/sso/callback route.ts:71, mail.ts:128, jobs.ts:157), users.totp_secret (auth/totp.ts:13,22), backup-code HMAC keyed by env.secret (auth/totp.ts:41-44, verified in actions/auth.ts:296) and the DNS proof value (auth/domain-proof.ts:22-24 used in actions/settings.ts:108,122, actions/platform.ts:102, jobs.ts:287 with DOMAIN_PROOF_GRACE_DAYS=7). README:311 confirms 'APP_SECRET is data'. No branch changes crypto.ts (grep keyId|rotat|APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS over diffs: no code hits).
- Smallest fix: One previous key, not a KMS. env.ts: optional APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS (min 32). crypto.ts: keys() = [current, previous?]; kid(secret) = sha256(secret).slice(0,8); encryptSecret writes 'v2:<kid>:iv:tag:data'; decryptSecret picks the key by kid for v2 and tries every key for v1 ciphertexts. totp.ts hashBackupCode: compute with the current key, and actions/auth.ts:296 loop also tries the previous-key hash (the legacyBackupHash pattern already there). domain-proof.ts: derive the TXT value from a separate stable key, key('domain-proof') of the FIRST key the installation ever had is not knowable, so simplest: domainProofRecord(tenantId, env.domainProofSecret) where env.domainProofSecret = APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET ?? APP_SECRET, documented as 'set it once and never rotate'; during an APP_SECRET rotation jobs.ts:287 and the two settings/platform checks accept either key's value. Add scripts/rotate-secret.ts: walks tenants.settings (the four *Enc fields) and users.totp_secret, decrypts with any key, re-encrypts with the current one, so APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS can be removed afterwards; README 'Operations notes' gets the four-step rotation. Tests: tests/crypto.test.ts (v1 still decrypts, v2 kid routing, rotate script on an in-memory DB).
- Files: portal/src/server/env.ts, portal/src/server/crypto.ts, portal/src/server/auth/totp.ts, portal/src/server/actions/auth.ts, portal/src/server/auth/domain-proof.ts, portal/src/server/actions/settings.ts, portal/src/server/actions/platform.ts, portal/src/server/jobs.ts, portal/scripts/rotate-secret.ts, portal/README.md, portal/.env.example, portal/tests/crypto.test.ts
- Risk: A bug in decryptSecret fallback silently turns every integration secret into null (mail.ts:128 would send with an empty password); the v1 path must stay byte-identical and be covered by a fixture ciphertext in the test. Existing TXT records must keep verifying after the change (fixture for the current derivation). signValue/unsignValue (crypto.ts:44-56) sign cookies/links with key('sign'); after rotation old signed values become invalid, which is acceptable (sessions re-sign in) but must be stated.

- Needs the owner: Nothing to build it; a rotation itself needs the owner to set APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS and run the script on each instance.

### D-06 · medium · partial (tests) · effort S
**The content library is imported at every start and a single bad file stops the server**

- Sources: audit:D-06
- Detail: bootstrap.ts L90-L112, library.ts L67-L101, instrumentation.ts L21-L28: 1,060 lesson files are read, validated and upserted in one advisory-locked transaction on each production start; any schema, integrity or parity error exits the process; content changes require a new image. Do not add skip-and-alert: silently serving a partial library changes what learners see and the full-transaction rollback (bootstrap.ts:24) is the safer behaviour. The 'import only when the content hash changes' part is premature: measure the start-up time of the import once in the AUD-1 compose job (log line bootstrap.ts:95 with a timestamp) and only if it exceeds the 60 s start-period (Dockerfile:48) add `where scenes is distinct from excluded.scenes` to the onConflictDoUpdate at library.ts:162-165.

### TST-13 · medium · open (tests) · effort S
**CI never touches real PostgreSQL, the pg driver, the migrate scripts or the Docker image**

- Sources: tests:TST-13
- Detail: Every DB-backed test boots an in-memory PGlite and applies drizzle/0000_init.sql (tests/helpers/db.ts testDb()); jobs-runner.test.ts fakes the pg pool entirely. scripts/migrate.ts, scripts/migrate.mjs and scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh (the production start path) and `docker build` are not run anywhere in ci.yml, and there is no drizzle-kit check/generate --check step, so the audit's High finding ('database migration regenerated from scratch on each schema change → an upgraded server would crash on start') cannot be caught by CI. The workflow comment 'the tests run against an in-memory PGlite database' is accurate but is the whole story.
- Evidence: tests.diff L1-84 (.github/workflows/ci.yml, new on the tests branch; main has no .github/ directory at all): job `checks` runs eslint, typecheck, check-lesson-locales and `vitest run`; job `build` runs `npm run build`. No `services: postgres`, no `scripts/migrate.mjs` or `scripts/migrate.ts` run, no `docker build`, no drizzle-kit step. Production start path scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh:72-73 (`node scripts/migrate.mjs`) and scripts/migrate.mjs:40-54 (pg pool) are therefore never executed anywhere. One correction to the finding: tests/helpers/db.ts (tests.diff L812-816) and every existing DB test on main (e.g. portal/tests/auth-security.test.ts:74) call `migrate(drizzle(pglite), { migrationsFolder: drizzle })`, i.e. the drizzle migrator replays the whole journal, not 0000_init.sql by name, so the demo branch's 0001/0002 are covered by the test database too; but it is still PGlite, and the 'regenerated 0000 crashes an upgraded server' scenario cannot be caught because no job ever migrates a database twice.
- Smallest fix: On the tests branch's .github/workflows/ci.yml: (1) in job `checks` add `services: postgres: image: postgres:16-alpine, env: POSTGRES_USER/PASSWORD/DB portal, ports: [5432:5432], options: --health-cmd pg_isready ...`, and after Install add two steps with `DATABASE_URL: postgres://portal:portal@localhost:5432/portal`: `node scripts/migrate.mjs` (the production path) and `node scripts/migrate.mjs` again (must be a no-op; this is the upgrade test the audit asked for); (2) add a drift step `npx drizzle-kit generate && git diff --exit-code --stat -- drizzle` (fails when schema.ts changed without a committed migration; `drizzle-kit check` only validates snapshot consistency, keep it as a cheap extra); (3) in job `build` add `docker build --pull -t portal .` (working-directory portal). Running vitest against PostgreSQL is not possible without refactoring: tests construct `new PGlite()` directly (helpers/db.ts:19, drill-service.test.ts:16); skip that.
- Files: .github/workflows/ci.yml
- Risk: CI time (+5-8 min for docker build; Docker Hub pulls on GitHub runners can hit the anonymous rate limit the demo session mentioned, so `--pull` of node and postgres images may need a registry login secret or GHCR mirror). The drift step depends on which migration policy wins (DMO-1): with the regenerate policy `generate` still yields no file when schema and snapshot agree, so it works either way.
- Depends on: DMO-1
- Needs the owner: Nothing; optionally a Docker Hub token as a repository secret if pulls get rate-limited.

Other compose notes: fixed public APP_SECRET and DB password (documented 'THROWAWAY ONLY'); the seed service builds the Dockerfile's `builder` target, which runs the full `next build` just to get tsx; the seed truncates every table on each `up`; port published on 127.0.0.1 only (good); no separate jobs worker (JOBS_ENABLED=1 in-process). The session's 'Docker Hub rate-limit workaround (repo Dockerfile unchanged)' is not visible anywhere in the diff.
- Evidence: Demo worktree portal/docker-compose.demo.yml: L13 DATABASE_URL in x-demo-env, L37 seed built from `target: builder`, L43 ALLOW_SEED: "1", L45 command `npx tsx scripts/migrate.ts && npx tsx scripts/seed.ts`, L51 app `condition: service_completed_successfully`; no SEED_PASSWORD anywhere in the file. Security worktree portal/scripts/seed-data.ts:16-24 `seedPasswordProblem`: with DATABASE_URL set and SEED_PASSWORD unset or equal to the published value it returns an error; seed.ts:43-46 prints 'Refusing to seed' and exits 1. Both branches touch seed.ts in different hunks (security @@ -28/-39/-52, demo @@ -136), so git merges them cleanly and the result is: seed container exits 1, app never starts. Main's own docker-compose.yml seed tool (L84-104, env_file .env) breaks the same way unless the operator sets their own SEED_PASSWORD in .env, which is the intended behaviour of H-1 and already documented in the security branch's .env.example hunk. The Dockerfile builder stage (main Dockerfile:93-98) runs `npm run build` before the seed can use tsx; main's compose worker service (L56-60) does the same, so it is the house pattern. 'Docker Hub rate-limit workaround' is not in any diff; the session said the Dockerfile was unchanged, so it was sandbox-side.
- Smallest fix: In portal/docker-compose.demo.yml seed service environment (L41-43) add `SEED_PASSWORD: ${SEED_PASSWORD:-<a 12+ character demo value that is not the .env.example one>}` and in docs/DEMO.md 'With Docker instead' (L58-66) add one sentence: 'The Docker stack's administrator password is <that value> (override with SEED_PASSWORD in the shell)'. Nothing else: the local `npm run demo` path is exempt (seedPasswordProblem returns null without DATABASE_URL). Re-run `docker compose -f portal/docker-compose.demo.yml up --build` once after both branches merge to confirm. Leave the builder-stage seed image as is (same pattern as the worker service).
- Files: portal/docker-compose.demo.yml, docs/DEMO.md
- Risk: The demo stack's password becomes public in the compose file, the same class as its fixed APP_SECRET and DB password (loopback-only, 'THROWAWAY ONLY' header L6-9); acceptable. Alternative `${SEED_PASSWORD:?...}` keeps it private but breaks the one-command promise.
- Depends on: DMO-1
- Needs the owner: Pick the demo value (12+ characters, not the published one) or choose the required-variable form.

### DMO-9 · medium · open · effort S
**npm run demo wipes the local database by default and, on Windows, probably orphans next dev on Ctrl+C**

- Sources: demo:DMO-9
- Detail: scripts/demo.mjs step 3 (diff lines 2108-2115) runs `npm run db:reset`, which deletes portal/.data/pg (the developer's own PGlite data) unless --keep-data is passed; there is no confirmation. The only safety is the port check in step 1 (lines 2091-2095) for the chosen port: a dev server from the same folder on another port (or the :3100 presentation copy if it shares .data/pg) would still be running when the reset deletes and re-migrates the single-process PGlite directory. On win32 the dev server is spawned as `npx next dev` with shell: true (line 2154) and stopped with child.kill('SIGTERM') (lines 2156-2162): that kills cmd.exe, not the node process it started, so next dev keeps port 3000 and the PGlite lock and the next `npm run demo` fails with 'Port 3000 is in use'. The owner's machine is Windows. The `--prod` path copies .data/pg into .next/standalone/.data/pg, sets ALLOW_EMBEDDED_DB=1 and a random APP_SECRET per run (line 2147) unless exported, so anything encrypted under the dev fallback key in the seeded DB would not decrypt in that run.
- Evidence: Demo worktree portal/scripts/demo.mjs: L101-106 `npm run db:reset` is the default unless `--keep-data`, no prompt; db:reset (package.json:16) deletes .data/pg. L83-87 checks only the chosen port. L47, L110 and L146 spawn with `shell: process.platform === "win32"`; L148 and L153 stop with `child.kill("SIGTERM")`. On Windows that terminates cmd.exe only (signals are ignored, TerminateProcess on the direct child); npx -> node -> `next dev` and its forked server process survive, holding the port and the PGlite directory, so the next run fails at L83 'Port 3000 is in use'. Two corrections: (a) the :3100 presentation copy does NOT share .data/pg: .claude/launch.json L18-21 runs scratchpad/demo/launch-demo.mjs, which chdir's into its own scratchpad/demo/portal with its own .data (launch-demo.mjs L1-8); only `npm run dev` or another demo started from the repo's portal/ folder on a different port is at risk. (b) the --prod random APP_SECRET (L139) is harmless for the seeded database: seed.ts stores nothing encrypted (no encrypt/TOTP/SMTP calls, grep empty) and sessions are sha256 of the token (src/server/auth/session.ts:18, demo-session.ts), so the warm-up session still validates; it only matters if someone saves SMTP/SSO secrets in a --prod demo and restarts without exporting APP_SECRET, which the script already honours.
- Smallest fix: demo.mjs: (1) invert the default at L101: `if (fs.existsSync(.data/pg) && !flag("reset")) { migrate } else { reset }`, rename the option in the header comment L11, DEMO.md option table L39-43 and the sentence 'Running the command again gives a fresh organisation' (DEMO.md L45), and the package.json row in portal/README.md L93; (2) replace `stop` at L148 with a win32 branch: `process.platform === "win32" ? spawnSync("taskkill", ["/pid", String(child.pid), "/T", "/F"]) : child.kill("SIGTERM")` and use the same in L42 and L153 (`/T` is what reaches next dev's forked server; spawning node directly without a shell, as launch-demo.mjs does, is not enough on its own). (3) One line in DEMO.md Troubleshooting: 'do not run it while any server from this folder is up'.
- Files: portal/scripts/demo.mjs, docs/DEMO.md, portal/README.md
- Risk: Flipping the default changes the presenter's promise of a fresh organisation on every run (they must pass --reset); taskkill /F gives next dev no chance to flush, which is fine for a dev server. No tests cover demo.mjs (it is a launcher with Node built-ins only).
- Depends on: 
- Needs the owner: Which default matters more: fresh organisation each run (presenter) or never deleting .data/pg silently (developer). Both are one flag.

### L-4 · low · partial (security) · effort S
**SMS gateway over plain HTTP accepted silently**

- Sources: security:L-4
- Detail: SMS_WEBHOOK_URL is validated only as z.url() (env.ts:52); sms.ts posts each sign-in code and SMS_WEBHOOK_TOKEN as a bearer header to it, so an http:// gateway sends codes and the token unencrypted. Branch hunk (env.ts, inside the `NODE_ENV === "production" && !building` block): `if (data.SMS_WEBHOOK_URL?.startsWith("http://")) console.warn("[env] SMS_WEBHOOK_URL uses plain http://: ...")`; .env.example now says to use https://; env.test.ts asserts the warning for http and its absence for https. Half-done by design and in detail: it is a warning, not a refusal; it fires only in production; and the check is a case-sensitive prefix, so `HTTP://host` passes silently.
- Evidence: Main portal/src/server/env.ts:52 `SMS_WEBHOOK_URL: z.preprocess(blank, z.url().optional())` accepts any scheme; portal/src/server/sms.ts:28-32 POSTs {to,text} with `authorization: Bearer ${SMS_WEBHOOK_TOKEN}` to it. security.diff env.ts hunk (@@ -101,6 +101,11 @@, inside the `NODE_ENV === "production" && !building` block after the TRUST_PROXY warning at main L99-103) adds `if (data.SMS_WEBHOOK_URL?.startsWith("http://")) console.warn(...)`: a warning, production only, case-sensitive prefix (zod keeps the original string, so `HTTP://host` or `Http://` passes silently). security.diff .env.example hunk (@@ -37,7 +37,8) documents https; tests/env.test.ts hunk (@@ -55,6 +55,17) asserts the warning for http and its absence for https. Nothing is deployed yet (audit: never deployed), so no installation depends on a plain-HTTP gateway today.
- Smallest fix: On the security branch's env.ts hunk, replace the warning with a refusal that reuses the existing opt-out instead of adding a new variable: `if (data.SMS_WEBHOOK_URL && new URL(data.SMS_WEBHOOK_URL).protocol !== "https:" && data.ALLOW_HTTP_APP_URL !== "1") throw new Error("SMS_WEBHOOK_URL must use https:// in production (sign-in codes and SMS_WEBHOOK_TOKEN travel in it); set ALLOW_HTTP_APP_URL=1 only for a plain-HTTP intranet or test stack.")` (the same semantics appUrlProblem gives APP_URL at env.ts:72-83, so the docker-compose.demo.yml stack with ALLOW_HTTP_APP_URL=1 keeps working). Update the two assertions in tests/env.test.ts ('warns when the SMS gateway is plain http' becomes rejects/accepts, plus one `HTTP://` case) and the .env.example comment L39-41. If the owner prefers to keep it a warning, the one-line change is only `new URL(url).protocol !== "https:"` in place of `startsWith("http://")`.
- Files: portal/src/server/env.ts, portal/tests/env.test.ts, portal/.env.example
- Risk: A future intranet installation with an https APP_URL and an http gateway must set ALLOW_HTTP_APP_URL=1, which also loosens the APP_URL check; acceptable because both describe the same trust class (a non-public stack). No data or callers affected.
- Depends on: 
- Needs the owner: Decide warn vs refuse now (nothing is deployed, so refusing costs nothing today).

**Session-stated follow-ups: embedded-DB lock out of scope, Docker Hub workaround unexplained, sixth session unknown**

- Detail: The session's final message lists as out of scope 'a lock on the embedded database so two local servers can never share it (touches core db client)', which is exactly the failure mode demo.mjs and the troubleshooting table warn about (PGlite single-process; DEMO.md line 161). README:309, DECISIONS ADR-004 result (L23) and DEMO.md Troubleshooting L142 rely on humans remembering. (2) Admin guide: the finding's seed suggestion is wrong. seed.ts:171 `tourDone: true` is the learner onboarding tour; the admin guide is remembered only in the browser: portal/src/components/admin/admin-tour.tsx:40 `DONE_KEY = "cw.adminTour.done"`, :107 `localStorage.getItem(DONE_KEY)` starts it on first visit, :192 `localStorage.setItem(DONE_KEY, "1")`. The seed cannot suppress it; DEMO.md L36 ('close it with Esc') is the right instruction. (3) Docker Hub workaround: no diff touches the Dockerfile or compose images (postgres:16-alpine, node:24-trixie-slim); the session note says the repo was unchanged, so it was sandbox-side; nothing to verify in code. (4) 'Pushed despite CLAUDE.md': process breach against CLAUDE.md L17 ('Commit only when asked; never push'); no code change.
- Smallest fix: Only (1) needs code, in createDb()'s PGlite branch (client.ts:58): write `.data/pg/.lock` with `fs.writeFileSync(lock, String(process.pid), { flag: "wx" })`; on EEXIST read the pid, `process.kill(pid, 0)` to test liveness, throw `Error("The embedded database in .data/pg is open by process <pid>: stop it first (next dev, npm run demo, db:* scripts)")` if alive, overwrite if stale; unlink in `close` and in a `process.once("exit")` handler. About 15 lines, one test in portal/tests (write a dead pid to the lock, expect createDb to succeed and rewrite it; write the current pid, expect the throw). For (2) nothing (keep the Esc line); for (3) ask the session owner only if the Docker stack fails to pull on the owner's machine; for (4) nothing.
- Files: portal/src/server/db/client.ts, portal/tests/db-lock.test.ts, portal/README.md
- Risk: Core path: every local server and script goes through createDb. A crash leaves a stale lock (handled by the pid-alive check; Windows pid reuse is rare but possible, and the message tells the user to delete the file). next dev with webpack keeps one server process, so HMR does not re-open the database; `next build` never opens it (DATABASE_URL unset, NEXT_PHASE guard at client.ts:54-55). Production (pg driver) is untouched.
- Depends on: 
- Needs the owner: Nothing for the lock. For the Docker Hub note, only the original session owner knows what the workaround was; it is not needed for the merge.

### I-4 · info · open · effort S
**Docker base image pinned by tag, not digest**

Conflicting guidance on main: portal/README.md:175 and docs/build/DECISIONS.md ADR-033 §5 (L218) say build with `--pull` so the image 'brings the latest Node security release', and docs/build/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md item 23(c) relies on that for the Brotli CVE fix (Node >= 24.22.1).
- Smallest fix: One line: `FROM node:24-trixie-slim@sha256:<index digest> AS base` in portal/Dockerfile:4 (take the multi-arch index digest, e.g. `docker buildx imagetools inspect node:24-trixie-slim`, not a single-platform digest). Then reword portal/README.md:175 and OPEN-QUESTIONS 23(c) from `--pull` to 'Dependabot proposes the digest bump weekly; merge it to pick up Node security releases'. Optionally the same for `postgres:16-alpine` in both compose files (Dependabot docker-compose ecosystem is configured at security.diff L74-88).

- Risk: With a pinned digest, Node patch releases (the Brotli CVE class) reach the image only when the owner merges the weekly Dependabot PR; with `--pull` they arrive on every build but the build is not reproducible. A wrong (single-platform) digest fails builds on the other architecture.
- Depends on: 
- Needs the owner: The policy choice above (reproducible digest + merge Dependabot weekly, versus `--pull` latest patch), and the digest value itself must be read from the registry at change time (needs Docker and network; not run here).
