No prettier config exists in portal/ on either side, so nothing enforces either style. Effect: the real change is unreviewable in the raw diff, and every future branch that touches schema.ts (the unknown sixth session, the planned SCORM/market-pack work) will conflict on every line.
- Evidence: The whole-file diff is real but the diagnosis is wrong: it is a line-ending flip, not a formatter. `git diff --numstat 683f272 HEAD -- portal/src/server/db/schema.ts` in the demo worktree = 1077/1032; `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --numstat` = 45/0 (same as `-w`); main's blob has 1,032 of 1,032 lines ending in CR (`git show 683f272:... | cat -A | grep -c '^M$'` = 1032) and the demo blob 0 of 1,077; `git ls-files --eol` on main lists portal/src/server/db/schema.ts as i/crlf. The longest line is 195 characters on both sides and the line count is exactly main + 45, so nothing was re-flowed; the raw diff's '+' side still shows the multi-line `import {` block (diff lines 1036-1050). Main is mixed: 299 of 2,095 tracked files are CRLF, 22 of them under portal/src; the cloud session's editor normalised the one CRLF file it touched. The 45 real lines are the `DrillEventRow` type and the `drillRuns` table (schema.ts:860-904 on the branch). No prettier config on either side, as the finding says, but irrelevant. None of the other four branches touches schema.ts or any CRLF file (checked file by file against `git ls-files --eol`), so the flip conflicts with nothing in flight today.
- Smallest fix: Review the branch with `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol 683f272 <demo> -- portal/src/server/db/schema.ts` (45 lines) and merge it as is: the LF version matches the other 1,796 LF files and the owner's core.autocrlf=false keeps the working tree identical to the index. To stop the next cloud session repeating it on one of the remaining 298 CRLF files, add after all five branches are merged a one-line .gitattributes (`* text=auto`) and one whitespace-only commit from `git add --renormalize .` (reviewable as 0 lines with `-w`). If a literal 45-line diff is wanted instead, convert the branch's schema.ts back to CRLF (unix2dos) before merging; that keeps the mixed state.
- Files: portal/src/server/db/schema.ts, .gitattributes
- Risk: The renormalise commit touches 299 files: any branch cut before it that edits one of them (the unknown sixth session) gets a whole-file conflict once, resolved by taking the branch's content with LF endings. The demo migration files (drizzle/0001, 0002) are unaffected.
- Depends on: DMO-15
- Needs the owner: Nothing; the owner should know the sixth session may hit the renormalise commit.

### MIS-1 · medium · not_an_issue · effort M
**ARCHITECTURE.md claims mail-scanner detonations never create false clicks, contradicting audit M-09**

- Sources: MIS-1
- Detail: ARCHITECTURE.md section 9 states: requests whose user agent or prefetch headers look like a mail security gateway are not counted, and 'Safe Links and sandbox detonations therefore do not create false clicks'. AUDIT.md M-09 (lines 398-402) states the opposite: a click is recorded on a plain GET of /t/{token}, scanners are recognised only by user-agent keywords, and a scanner that detonates links with a browser user agent creates a 'phishing click' risk against an innocent employee. The customer-facing architecture document therefore overstates the integrity of the risk score; DOC-22 covers other inaccuracies in ARCHITECTURE.md but not this one.
- Evidence: The comparison mismatch is unreachable. Every e-mail entry point validates with zod 4.6.7 z.email() (portal/package.json:44), whose default pattern (portal/node_modules/zod/v4/core/regexes.js:34, applied at schemas.js:207) is ASCII-only with a `[A-Za-z]{2,}$` top-level label: sign-in auth.ts:203/:250/:267/:436, SSO callback route.ts:20/:79 (an IdP claim user@пример.рф fails as no_email_claim before :109), people add people.ts:58, import people.ts:525, operator tenant creation platform.ts:35. So emailDomain() (sso-routing.ts:27-31) never sees a Unicode domain, and a punycode IDN TLD (xn--p1ai) is refused too. For an IDN label under an ASCII TLD (пример.com → xn--e1afmkfd.com, which main's HOST regex at domain-proof.ts:13 already accepts in punycode) the only enterable form is user@xn--e1afmkfd.com, which emailDomain returns as-is and which equals the stored value, so the foreign-domain guards at people.ts:123/:528 and the SSO checks hold. No branch touches emailDomain (grep of all five diffs). Real residual, different finding: on the tests branch a tenant can prove пример.рф (normaliseHost → xn--e1afmkfd.xn--p1ai, tests.diff domain-proof.ts hunk) but nobody with an address on that domain can be added, imported or signed in, because z.email() refuses both forms.
- Smallest fix: Nothing for the stated bug. If IDN e-mail addresses are to be supported: (1) pass a pattern to every z.email() that accepts punycode labels (`xn--` TLD), and (2) make emailDomain() return domainToASCII(part after '@') with normaliseHost's guard so the stored ASCII form matches; add one case to tests/password-domain.test.ts and the SSO routing test. Without (1), (2) is dead code.
- Files: portal/src/server/auth/sso-routing.ts, portal/src/server/actions/auth.ts, portal/src/server/actions/people.ts, portal/src/app/api/sso/callback/[tenant]/route.ts, portal/src/server/actions/platform.ts, portal/tests/password-domain.test.ts
- Risk: Relaxing z.email() widens what reaches mail sending and SSO; must keep the domainToASCII guard so 'a/b' or query strings cannot become a domain.
- Depends on: 
- Needs the owner: Whether IDN e-mail addresses (user@пример.рф) must be accepted at all; today the tests branch's IDN domain proof is only usable for IDN labels under ASCII TLDs.

- Detail: The roadmap assumes the founder plus one senior full-stack engineer (contract from day 1, permanent by day 60), both using the AI-agent workflow with human review on every merge; each phase is about 11-13 engineer-weeks per 30 days. With the founder alone the plan stretches to 120-150 days. Roadmap risk table: founder bandwidth across product, engineering, sales, content and legal.
- Evidence: `docs/ROADMAP.md:18` (audit worktree): "The plan assumes the founder plus one senior full-stack engineer (contract from day 1, permanent hire by day 60), both using the AI-agent workflow ... Each phase is about 11–13 ew ... With the founder alone, keep the order and stretch the p[lan]"; `docs/ROADMAP.md:146` risk row "Founder bandwidth: product, engineering, sales, content and legal in one person" with mitigation "Contract the second engineer in week 1". Repository facts: one human author on main (git shortlog, 9 commits 2026-10-19 to 2026-11-05); in one day the five cloud sessions produced 12,570 diff lines (wc -l of the five diffs) that nobody has reviewed yet, which shows the throughput the assumption relies on and that review, not writing, is the bottleneck. A planning assumption, not a defect; nothing in code closes it.
- Smallest fix: No code change. Owner either contracts the engineer in week 1 (roadmap 1.8) or re-baselines the roadmap to 120-150 days by editing `docs/ROADMAP.md:18` and the phase dates; merging the tests branch CI first makes either path safer because every later merge gets automatic checks.
- Files: docs/ROADMAP.md
- Risk: Without a second reviewer the five pending branches (security, tests, docs, demo, audit) merge on AI review alone, which is exactly the O-01 condition the roadmap wants to end.
- Depends on: O-01
- Needs the owner: Decide hire-now vs founder-alone timeline and budget; nothing else.

### DMO-6 · low · open · effort S
**Polling cost and GET-with-side-effects: one request per second per open dashboard, each one applying events and running five queries**

- Sources: demo:DMO-6
- Detail: live-drill.tsx polls /api/admin/drill/[id] every POLL_MS = 1_000 (diff line 2644, 2692-2721) until status 'finished'; there is no backoff when the tab is hidden and no ETag/304. Each poll runs advanceDrill (select run, select campaign, lease CAS, then per applied non-deliver/open event an audienceRisk aggregate and, for report/train, recomputeRisk) plus drillView (recipients join users join departments, module, campaign) plus getLocale. Two viewers double it; on the single-process PGlite the dev server shares that connection. Both the route handler GET (route.ts line 2438-2447) and the RSC page render (page.tsx line 2356) mutate state. 'Skip to the end' applies every remaining event in one server action (up to ~6 events × 35 people, each with several writes) with the lease renewed per step.
- Evidence: Exists only on the demo branch (main has no drill). wt/demo portal/src/components/admin/drill/live-drill.tsx:19 `const POLL_MS = 1_000`; L67-96 the poll effect re-arms `setTimeout(poll, POLL_MS)` after every answer, fetches with `cache: "no-store"` (L73) and has no `visibilitychange`/`document.hidden` check and no ETag/If-None-Match; it stops only on status "finished" (L85) or 401/403/404 (L75). Route: src/app/api/admin/drill/[id]/route.ts:16-17 GET runs `advanceDrill` then `drillView` and answers no-store (L19). Page: src/app/(admin)/admin/drill/[id]/page.tsx:23 runs `advanceDrill` inside the RSC render. Service: src/server/services/drill.ts:205-273 advanceDrill = select run (L206), select campaign (L210), lease CAS (L219-223), per applied event applyEvent (L237) + CAS (L239-244) + `audienceRisk` aggregate for non-deliver/open (L252), recomputeRisk on report/train (L174,183); drillView L349; skipDrill L302-308 rewinds startedAt and applies every remaining event in one call. Two viewers double the work; PGlite is single-process in dev.
- Smallest fix: In live-drill.tsx `poll` (L71): `if (document.visibilityState === "hidden") { timer = setTimeout(poll, POLL_MS); return; }` and add a `visibilitychange` listener in the same effect that calls `poll()` once when the tab becomes visible (remove it in the cleanup). In page.tsx:23 replace `advanceDrill(db(), v.tenant.id, id)` with the `drillById` result already fetched at L20, so the render only reads; the first poll at POLL_MS/2 (L91) catches up. Keep writes in the route only. SSE and backoff are not needed for one presenter.
- Files: portal/src/components/admin/drill/live-drill.tsx, portal/src/app/(admin)/admin/drill/[id]/page.tsx
- Risk: A dashboard opened after a long gap shows the pre-catch-up state for up to 500 ms; wt/demo tests/drill-service.test.ts exercise the service, not the page, so they stay green. Nothing blocking for the presentation copy.

### MIS-12 · low · open · effort S
**First-visit admin tour overlay covers the drill setup page**

- Sources: MIS-12
- Detail: The demo session reports that 'first-visit admin tour overlay blocked a Playwright click', and DEMO.md step 3 tells the presenter 'If the admin guide opens over the page, close it with Esc'. Because `npm run demo` rebuilds the organisation every run, the demo administrator is always a first-time visitor, so every demo starts by dismissing an overlay before the 0:00 talk-track step. The warm-up script (DMO-10) inserts a session but does not mark the tour as seen.
- Evidence: tests worktree portal/tests/helpers/db.ts:18-23 and demo worktree portal/tests/drill-service.test.ts:15-24 both `new PGlite()` + `migrate(..., { migrationsFolder: drizzle })`; ci.yml:53-54 runs only vitest. Main has 16 more tests doing the same (grep migrationsFolder), none reads _journal.json (grep of main, tests and demo test folders: no hit). Migrator rule in node_modules/drizzle-orm/pg-core/dialect.js:57-67: applies every entry whose folderMillis is greater than the last `created_at` in __drizzle_migrations, so a regenerated 0000_init with a newer `when` re-runs its CREATE TABLEs on an existing database, and a changed 0000 with the same `when` is silently skipped (drift). The container runs node scripts/migrate.mjs at every start (portal/scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh:18-19, Dockerfile:50), so that is the crash loop. Main and demo journals both keep idx 0 tag 0000_init when 1793051964708; demo adds idx 1-2 without touching 0000_init.sql (demo stat). docs branch ARCHITECTURE.md:210 and README.md:272 still document regeneration; ROADMAP.md:69 item 1.5 asks for 'CI proves an upgrade from the previous release's schema'.
- Smallest fix: New portal/tests/migrations-journal.test.ts (no database): read drizzle/meta/_journal.json and assert entries[0] equals {idx 0, tag '0000_init', when 1793051964708}, idx is sequential, `when` strictly increases, every tag has drizzle/<tag>.sql, and sha256 of drizzle/0000_init.sql equals a pinned constant (catches a regenerated or edited baseline whether or not `when` changed). The full upgrade test (apply a tagged previous release's drizzle folder, then the current one) is ROADMAP 1.5 and waits for a first release tag.
- Files: portal/tests/migrations-journal.test.ts
- Risk: The test fails on purpose when anyone regenerates 0000_init, which the docs branch still describes as the convention; the constant must be changed deliberately with a migration review.

### TST-16 · medium · partial (tests) · effort S
**senderDomain still rejects internationalised domains, so the IDN proof cannot be used for branded mail**

- Sources: tests:TST-16
- Detail: src/server/actions/settings.ts:58-63 validates branding.senderDomain with /^([a-z0-9-]+\.)+[a-z]{2,}$|^$/i — a TLD of letters only — so both 'пример.рф' and 'example.xn--p1ai' are refused by saveBrandingAction after the branch made normaliseHost accept them. src/server/mail.ts:117 treats the sender as proven only when normaliseHost(branding.senderDomain) === tenant.domain, so an organisation whose proven domain is now stored as 'xn--e1afmkfd.xn--p1ai' can never set a matching sender domain and always falls back to the platform sender. Also still ASCII-only: the IOC email classifier in src/server/actions/secops.ts:287 and the EMAIL regex in src/server/sandbox/analyze.ts:266 (addresses under an IDN TLD are not recognised as emails).
- Evidence: Main: portal/src/server/actions/settings.ts:58-63 senderDomain `.regex(/^([a-z0-9-]+\.)+[a-z]{2,}$|^$/i)` (TLD letters only: 'example.xn--p1ai' and 'пример.рф' both fail); mail.ts:117 `proven = … normaliseHost(tenant.branding.senderDomain) === tenant.domain`; secops.ts:287 `/^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[a-z]{2,}$/i`; sandbox/analyze.ts:266 `const EMAIL = /@(?<=([a-z0-9._%+-]+)@)[a-z0-9.-]+\.[a-z]{2,}/gi`; domain-proof.ts:13 HOST on main still `[a-z]{2,63}` (so on main the IDN proof itself is also refused). Tests branch: tests.diff:210-224 new HOST `(?:[a-z]{2,63}|xn--[a-z0-9-]{1,59})` + domainToASCII in normaliseHost; tests.diff:1917-1921 asserts 'пример.рф' → 'xn--e1afmkfd.xn--p1ai'; tests.diff touches only domain-proof.ts among these files (grep diff --git: L194) and contains no 'senderDomain'; CHANGELOG at tests.diff:112-116 claims the markets' domains are accepted. So after the tests branch a tenant.domain can be 'xn--e1afmkfd.xn--p1ai' while saveBrandingAction can never store a matching senderDomain: the proven path at mail.ts:117 is unreachable for IDN tenants.
- Smallest fix: settings.ts:58-63: replace the regex with `.refine((v) => v === "" || normaliseHost(v) !== null).transform((v) => (v ? normaliseHost(v)! : v))` (import normaliseHost from ../auth/domain-proof) so the stored value is the ASCII form mail.ts:117 compares; secops.ts:287 and analyze.ts:266 change `[a-z]{2,}` to `(?:[a-z]{2,}|xn--[a-z0-9-]+)`; add a test in portal/tests/password-domain.test.ts (tests branch) saving 'пример.рф' as senderDomain and asserting sendMail picks `no-reply@xn--e1afmkfd.xn--p1ai`, plus one IOC 'user@пример.xn--p1ai' classified as email.
- Files: portal/src/server/actions/settings.ts, portal/src/server/actions/secops.ts, portal/src/server/sandbox/analyze.ts, portal/tests/password-domain.test.ts
- Risk: analyze.ts:266 is written against quadratic scanning (lookbehind, comment L262-265): the TLD alternation stays anchored after the '@' so it remains linear, but keep the pattern shape. Existing tenants with an ASCII senderDomain are unaffected; the branding form shows the xn-- form back to the admin (acceptable, or display via domainToUnicode).

- Needs the owner: Nothing.

Server: only 10 call sites use transactions; launchCampaign (campaigns.ts L71-L107) sets a campaign to running before inserting recipients one by one; attestModule (progress.ts L207-L228) writes attestation, module status and certificate as three separate writes; createAssignmentAction (workspace.ts L184-L260); attestations and certificates have no unique key per user and module (schema.ts L476-L503), so two concurrent attest calls can issue two certificates.
  [tests:TST-4] Root cause (diff, progress.ts attestModule): select module_progress.status, bail unless 'awaiting_attestation', insert attestation, update status — two concurrent confirmations both passed the check, giving two attestation rows and two certificate serials for the same module (compliance evidence double-counted). Fix: inside db.transaction, UPDATE module_progress SET status='completed', completedAt, percent=100 WHERE userId/moduleId AND status='awaiting_attestation' RETURNING claims the transition, and only the claimant inserts the attestation in the same transaction (completion and its text are atomic); issueCertificate() runs after commit because its duplicate-serial retry would fail inside an aborted transaction. Regression tests: two concurrent attestModule calls → one non-null result, one attestation, one certificate; a later attestation is refused. Sibling left open: the learning-path certificate in actions/learning.ts is still check-then-insert (TST-14).

Not on any branch: unique keys on attestations/certificates (demo.diff:5115-5127 shows the certificates table unchanged in its whole-file rewrite), createAssignmentAction (workspace.ts has transactions only at :95 and :145), and the client-side result-shape/catch consolidation (outside this area, not verified).

The attestation claim already makes the module path safe; the index is the backstop. Client part (one ActionResult + shared helper, segment error.tsx) is roadmap 3.5 and separate.

### TST-3 · high · fixed_on_branch (tests) · effort S
**A lesson completion sent twice at the same moment awarded its XP twice**

- Sources: tests:TST-3
- Detail: Root cause (diff, portal/src/server/services/progress.ts completeLesson): the code selected the lesson_progress row, computed firstTime = !existing?.completedAt, then upserted with xpAwarded + xp; two concurrent requests (double submit, retry) both read no completedAt, both awarded XP and both called awardXp(), doubling users.xp, xp_events and the league/level. - Detail: completeLessonAction (portal/src/server/actions/learning.ts:91-148) stores the browser's answers[].correct, firstTry and outcome as evidence and emits a 'simulation.risky' webhook/syslog event whenever an outcome is not 'safe' (lines 124-141): any learner can send up to 60 such events per 10 minutes to the customer's SIEM naming any module and lesson key. `seconds` (0-14,400 per call, line 102) is summed into secondsSpent, the time-trained figure in reports. Studio authors (allowed(v,'studio.write'), line 27) can complete and attest unpublished drafts and earn XP and certificates for them. Policy sign-off (policies.ts, password-verified) and labs (engage.ts, server-scored with a row lock) are sound; path certificates follow module completion (TST-14). The server-side check planned in OWN-3/DMO-11 must therefore validate answers and outcomes, not only completion.
- Evidence: Main portal/src/server/actions/learning.ts:19-31 moduleBySlug skips the published filter for `allowed(v, "studio.write")` and :33-46 attestModuleAction, :112-148 completeLessonAction use it, so authors earn XP, attestations and path certificates (:42,65) on drafts; :91-104 schema takes correct/firstTry/outcome and seconds 0..14400 from the browser; :117 rate limit 60 per 10 min; :124-141 stores the answers and emits simulation.risky for any non-safe outcome (events.ts:10-19 queues it to the tenant's webhook and syslog when the tenant subscribed to that event; tenant-defaults.ts:209 lists it); :143 passes seconds to completeLesson, which sums them (tests.diff progress.ts hunk still `secondsSpent + p.secondsSpent`, uncapped). Nuance: lessonKey must belong to the module (:120-122), so the event names a real module/lesson of the learner's choosing, not an arbitrary string. Audit S-01 (AUDIT.md:197, :471) and ROADMAP 1.2 (:66) cover answers/outcomes; the draft and seconds points are not in any branch.
- Smallest fix: Now, independent of OWN-3: in completeLessonAction and attestModuleAction return `{ ok: true, xp: 0 }` / `{ ok: false }` without writing when `mod.status !== "published"` (preview still plays, nothing is earned), and cap `secondsSpent: Math.min(p.data.seconds, lesson.minutes * 180)` at learning.ts:143; add two cases to tests/learning-actions.test.ts (tests branch). Deriving correct/outcome from lesson_contents belongs to the server-side completion check (OWN-3 / ROADMAP 1.2) and must include the simulation.risky emit at :141.
- Files: portal/src/server/actions/learning.ts, portal/tests/learning-actions.test.ts
- Risk: Studio authors lose XP/certificates for draft previews (intended); the cap changes 'time trained' only for inputs above 3x the lesson's nominal minutes; existing self-reported rows stay as they are.
- Depends on: OWN-3
- Needs the owner: Whether a studio author's draft preview should record any progress at all, and the cap factor (3x nominal minutes proposed).

## legal-content-ownership (5)

### L-01 · critical · open · effort M
**Legal texts name the wrong AI processor and lack the provider's identity**

- Sources: audit:L-01, repo:REP-19, repo:REP-8
- Detail: [audit:L-01] All 20 files in portal/content/legal (e.g. privacy.en.md L8, L57, L70, L79, L163-L164; terms.en.md L8, L43, L58, L93) state that AI Sel's answers are generated by Google Gemini through Google Cloud Vertex AI and processed in Google data centres; the code sends lesson text and questions to Anthropic (tutor, subtitles, studio) and narration to ElevenLabs. The provider's legal name, registration number, address and privacy contact are '[to be provided]'. The policy describes data the demo form does not collect (role, source, test score) and promises deletion of demo requests after 24 months, which no job implements. No DPA template or sub-processor list. Flagged by the team in OPEN-QUESTIONS.md items 8 and 20, unresolved. A customer cannot sign a contract or DPA on these texts.
  [repo:REP-19] Leftover from the original Cylosof text. grep shows 3 Vertex mentions in every privacy.{lang}.md (en: lines 57 §5.1, 70 §6, 79 §7.2) and 1 in every terms.{lang}.md (en: line 93 §10.1 'Google Gemini models through Google Cloud Vertex AI'): 40 mentions in 20 files. In this portal AI Sel runs on the Anthropic Claude API (ADR-008), AI captions send lesson text to Anthropic (ADR-029), ElevenLabs receives lesson text only when clips are generated (ADR-028), and spoken questions use the browser's speech recognition (Google service in Chrome). The text must not be changed without the owner's approval; the audit branch rates this Critical.
  [repo:REP-8] Privacy Policy and Terms exist in ten languages but the Provider's company name, registration number, address and contact address are placeholders: privacy.en.md lines 8, 38, 121, 163 and 164 ('[to be provided]'). The translations were made by AI agents, so each language needs a lawyer (ideally one who knows that country's law). Which lawyer and which languages first is undecided.
- Evidence: Main checkout. Wrong processor: portal/content/legal/privacy.en.md L57 (§5.1 'Google Cloud Vertex AI'), L59 (§5.3 voice recording 'sent to Google'), L61 (§5.5 Google terms), L70 (§6.3 sub-processor bullet 'Google Cloud … Vertex AI'), L79 (§7.2 'Google Vertex AI … Google data centres'); portal/content/legal/terms.en.md L93 (§10.1 'Google Gemini models through Google Cloud Vertex AI'). grep -c vertex|gemini: 3 in every privacy.{10 langs}.md, 1 in every terms.{10}.md = 40 mentions / 20 files. Actual code: portal/package.json L22 only '@anthropic-ai/sdk' (no google/vertex dependency); portal/src/server/env.ts L25-29 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_MODEL/ANTHROPIC_TUTOR_MODEL; portal/src/server/ai.ts L2,L74 `new Anthropic(...)` (studio drafts); portal/src/server/tutor.ts L207 `Anthropic.MessageStreamParams` with lesson context L38 + cache_control L221; portal/src/server/subtitles.ts L2 Anthropic; portal/src/lib/tts/key.ts L4 ElevenLabs clips; portal/src/components/player/tutor-panel.tsx L114-115,L131 browser SpeechRecognition/webkitSpeechRecognition (no recording leaves the Service). Placeholders: privacy.en.md L8 (x3), L38, L121, L163 (x3), L164; terms.en.md L8 (x3), L43, L58, L116, L170 (x3), L171; same positions in az ('sonradan göstəriləcək') and ru ('будет указан…'); 9-10 bracket placeholders in each of the other 8 languages. Data the form does not collect: privacy.en.md L38 promises storage of 'the role you selected, what brought you to the form and the level of your test score' and deletion after 24 months; portal/src/server/db/schema.ts L930-942 demo_requests has only name,email,organisation,country,employees,message,locale,consentVersion,status; portal/src/server/actions/site.ts L26-36 zod schema matches (no role/source/score). No deletion job: portal/src/server/jobs.ts cleanup() L351-374 purges loginAttempts, rateLimitBuckets, sessions, authTokens, watermarkCodes, outbox, webhookDeliveries, notifications only; demoRequests, tutor_cache (schema L1002) and ai_cache (schema L1013) are never purged and §8 (privacy.en.md L83-95) lists no retention for them. Extra inconsistency: privacy.en.md L165 §16.3 says the policy is published in az/en/ru while ten languages ship. No sub-processor list or DPA anywhere: `ls docs` = audit, build, business; no docs/legal. Branches: grep '^+++ b/portal/content/legal' in audit/security/tests/docs/demo .diff = 0 hits; audit.diff L443-447 only documents it, docs.diff L288-290 lists it in README as a known limitation, demo.diff L185 mentions OPEN-QUESTIONS 20. Nothing fixes it.
- Smallest fix: Two parts. (1) Code, so the text can be true: one line in portal/src/server/jobs.ts cleanup() after the notifications line: `total += await deleteInBatches(db, t.demoRequests, t.demoRequests.id, and(lt(t.demoRequests.createdAt, ago(730 * DAY))), deadline);` (or drop the 24-month sentence instead). (2) Text, same edits in all 20 portal/content/legal/{privacy,terms}.<lang>.md: privacy §3.3 remove the role/source/test-score clause; §5.1 'Google Cloud Vertex AI' -> 'the Anthropic API (Anthropic PBC, USA)', add that AI subtitles and Studio drafts send lesson text to the same provider; §5.3 spoken questions are converted to text by the browser's own speech engine (vendor depends on the browser), the Service receives text only; §5.4 add that narration clips are produced by ElevenLabs from lesson text only; §5.5 Anthropic commercial terms (no training on customer data); §6.3 replace the Google bullet with Anthropic (tutor, subtitles, studio) and ElevenLabs (narration); §7.2 Anthropic/ElevenLabs processing in the USA under their DPAs/SCCs; §8 add rows for tutor_cache/ai_cache (kept until the lesson is deleted) and demo requests 24 months; §16.3 ten languages; terms §10.1 'Claude models through the Anthropic API'. Bump the header `<!-- version: 3; effective: <date> -->` (read by portal/src/app/(site)/legal/[doc]/page.tsx L19-26) and set the demo form consentVersion (portal/src/lib/landing.ts L147, scenes.tsx L681) to the same date. Keep '[to be provided]' until the owner supplies the identity. New owner/counsel documents, not code: docs/legal/SUBPROCESSORS.md and docs/legal/DPA-template.md (en, az). No message keys change (site.legal namespace untouched).
- Files: portal/content/legal/privacy.{az,en,ru,tr,ro,ka,uk,de,fr,ar}.md, portal/content/legal/terms.{az,en,ru,tr,ro,ka,uk,de,fr,ar}.md, portal/src/server/jobs.ts, portal/src/lib/landing.ts, docs/legal/SUBPROCESSORS.md, docs/legal/DPA-template.md, docs/build/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md
- Risk: Legal wording changed by non-lawyers in ten languages; the owner said the text must not change without approval (OPEN-QUESTIONS 20). A new effective date changes the consentVersion recorded on new demo requests (harmless, it is stored per row). The 730-day purge deletes demo_requests rows including 'won' leads unless the status filter excludes them. The UpCloud/London hosting claims in §6.3/§7.1 cannot be verified from code.

### L-02 · critical · partial (docs) · effort S
**Intellectual-property chain of title for inherited lessons, mascot and design is undocumented**

- Sources: audit:L-02
- Detail: docs/audit/README.md states everything in docs/audit was extracted from the live cylosof.com portal through a demo tenant of a government agency. The scenes of all 106 English lessons shipped in portal/content/library are identical to the extracted originals (verified file by file; only the wrapper differs), public/rive/mascot.riv is byte-identical to the extracted asset, and the design tokens, landing copy and legal texts were carried over. The project skill calls cylosof.com the founder's own earlier product, but the repository contains no assignment, licence or ownership record and no LICENSE file. If any part belonged to a company, employer, co-founder or contractor, the core library is encumbered; investors will not close without this resolved.
- Evidence: Main checkout. Provenance: docs/audit/00-overview.md L3 'Mənbə: https://cylosof.com, demo tenant Rəqəmsal İnkişaf Agentliyi (rida)'; docs/audit/README.md L3 same. Verified identity: sha256 docs/audit/assets/mascot.riv == portal/public/rive/mascot.riv (943fa8440ec7…ea98a); a node comparison of every *.en.json under docs/audit/content/lessons against portal/content/library/lessons: total 106, scenes JSON-identical 106, different 0, missing 0. Also inherited: portal/content/policies/acceptable-use.{10}.md L1 header 'Source: https://cyclowareness.com/policies/1219e32b-… Version 1, published 03.10.2026'. No ownership record: `ls LICENSE* portal/LICENSE*` = none; portal/package.json has only '"private": true' (L4), no license field; git log --all --grep licen|assign|copyright|trademark finds no such commit; the only rights text is portal/messages/en/common.json L192 'All rights reserved.' Branches: docs.diff L336-338 adds a README '## Licence' section ('no licence file … grants no right … Contact Safarov Industries') = a notice only; audit.diff L457-459, L523 (O-06), L624 (roadmap 1.1) describe the gap; no diff adds a LICENSE file, an assignment or a chain-of-title record (grep 'chain of title' in security/tests/docs/demo diffs = 0).
- Smallest fix: Repo side (S): add root LICENSE ('Copyright (c) 2026 <owner entity>. All rights reserved. No licence is granted.'), add `"license": "UNLICENSED"` to portal/package.json, and add docs/build/CHAIN-OF-TITLE.md: one table row per inherited asset class (106 lessons in portal/content/library/lessons by module, portal/public/rive/mascot.riv, design tokens, landing copy, legal texts, the AUP from cyclowareness.com) with columns author / employer or contractor / agreement / evidence file, left as 'evidence needed' for the owner. Everything else is paper the owner provides (see needs_owner). Merging the docs branch brings the README notice but closes nothing on its own.
- Files: LICENSE, portal/package.json, docs/build/CHAIN-OF-TITLE.md, docs/build/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md
- Risk: No code risk. Legal risk: if any lesson, the mascot or the AUP text belonged to a company, co-founder or contractor, the 106-lesson library and mascot must be re-authored or assigned before an investor closes; a LICENSE naming the wrong entity would itself be a defect, so the entity name must come from the owner.
- Depends on: 
- Needs the owner: Who built cylosof.com and under which entity; IP assignment or employment/contractor agreements for lesson authors, translators, the Rive mascot artist and the original designer; company registration record; confirmation that cylosof.com and cyclowareness.com are owner-controlled; the entity name for the LICENSE.

Callers: live-drill.tsx:73 and :119 (fetch GET); skipDrillAction (actions/drill.ts:49) is a server action and already origin-checked by Next. Impact: only already-due synthetic events of the admin's own running drill; no attacker input beyond the id.
- Smallest fix: In route.ts: rename the current handler to `POST`, add `if (!sameOrigin(request)) return new Response('Forbidden', { status: 403 })` after apiViewer; add a read-only `GET` that returns `drillView(db(), await drillById(db(), v.tenant.id, id), locale)` (drillById exists, services/drill.ts:407). - Files: portal/src/app/api/admin/drill/[id]/route.ts, portal/src/components/admin/drill/live-drill.tsx, docs/API.md
- Risk: Any other poller of the GET would stop advancing the drill; only live-drill.tsx calls it. Behind a proxy the POST needs TRUST_PROXY set correctly for sameOrigin, as the other POST handlers already do.

## product-gap-strategic (19)

### M-02 · high · open · effort M
**Plans include features that are not built, and some settings do nothing**

- Sources: audit:M-02, docs:DOC-7, docs:DOC-6, repo:REP-4, repo:REP-14
- Detail: [audit:M-02] tenant-defaults.ts L286-L291: the Professional plan lists sso, ldap and sms_voice. Only OpenID Connect is implemented (sso/start/route.ts L17): SAML fields are stored (settings.ts L178-L214) but no SAML flow exists; LDAP settings including a bind password and certificate pin are saved but no LDAP client exists; voice campaigns have no telephony code and once VOICE_PROVIDER is set to any value they record every recipient as 'sent' without placing a call (campaigns.ts L43, L89-L104); SMS supports only a generic webhook (sms.ts); the 'Android screen block' setting has no Android app. No SCIM. A customer buying Professional for directory sync or voice phishing gets settings screens and delivery records for features that do not exist: misrepresentation and refund risk.
  [docs:DOC-7] README roadmap line 290 ('SAML sign-in and LDAP directory synchronisation. Their settings screens exist'), ARCHITECTURE.md section 5 line 206 ('SAML and LDAP settings can be saved, with their secrets encrypted, but no SAML exchange and no directory synchronisation are implemented') and section 17 line 490; API.md line 525 'SAML is not connected'. Code: portal/src/components/admin/settings-tabs.tsx lines 455-523 carry samlEntryPoint/samlCertificate and the saml protocol option, LDAP settings live in portal/src/lib/tenant-defaults.ts and portal/src/server/actions/settings.ts; portal/src/server/auth/sso-routing.ts line 17 'SAML is not connected'. Both 'sso' and 'ldap' are features of the professional plan (tenant-defaults.ts line 288), so a customer can buy a feature that does nothing.
  [docs:DOC-6] README line 84 ('the two voice-call templates still need a telephony adapter'), roadmap line 292, ARCHITECTURE.md section 9 line 316 ('Voice creates recipient rows only. No telephony adapter places calls yet') and section 17 line 489. Code: portal/src/server/services/campaigns.ts line 43 blocks a voice launch in production only when env.VOICE_PROVIDER is empty (portal/src/server/env.ts line 55 defines it as a free string); line 93 inserts recipients with sentAt: sms ? null : now, so voice recipients are stamped sent at launch, and line 295 counts sentAt as 'sent' in the funnel. portal/README.md line 114 describes VOICE_PROVIDER as 'Telephony provider for voice-call simulations', which implies setting it makes calls; nothing reads it except the gate. The docs branch wording understates this: rows are not merely created, they are reported as delivered. Voice templates are also sold as the sms_voice feature of the professional plan (portal/src/lib/tenant-defaults.ts line 288).

### M-04 · high · open · effort S
**Natural-voice narration has not been generated**

- Sources: audit:M-04, docs:DOC-15, repo:REP-2
- Detail: [audit:M-04] The ElevenLabs pipeline (scripts/generate-narration.ts) exists but no clips or manifests are in the repository (ADR-028, about USD 321 for all ten languages); without them lessons rely on the browser's voice, and Chrome on Windows has no Azerbaijani voice, so the home-market language is silent there.
  [docs:DOC-15] README Project status line 268 ('natural-voice narration, because no clips have been generated') and roadmap line 284 ('Choose a narration voice for each language and generate the ElevenLabs clips'); ARCHITECTURE.md section 7 line 260 and section 17 line 498. Confirmed: portal/public/generated/tts and portal/content/narration, the output paths named in portal/scripts/generate-narration.ts lines 9-10, do not exist in the checkout; README line 70 nonetheless lists 'Narration with word-by-word highlighting' as a feature (it works through Web Speech only).
  [repo:REP-2] Pipeline exists (ADR-028, scripts/generate-narration.ts) but no clip was ever generated: dry run on 2026-11-04 gave 37,724 clips / 4.01 M characters, ~321 USD (26-38 USD per language). ElevenLabs retires default voices on 2026-12-31, so ELEVENLABS_VOICE_<LOCALE> must be chosen by a native speaker per language (az, ka, ar first) after listening to one sample lesson. Until then Web Speech reads everything: on Chrome/Windows there is no Azerbaijani voice, so az lessons are silent with VoiceNotice and never auto-advance (lesson-engine gap 1, mascot gap 'Voice'); talkbody amplitude animations are never driven; tutor answers stay on Web Speech even with clips.
- Evidence: portal/scripts/generate-narration.ts:9-10 writes public/generated/tts/<locale>/<key>.mp3 and content/narration/<locale>/<module>__<lesson>.json; `ls portal/public/generated` and `ls portal/content/narration` both fail (No such file or directory) and `git ls-files` lists no clip or manifest (only the script, src/server/narration.ts and tests/narration.test.ts). portal/src/server/narration.ts:29-35 returns null on ENOENT, so the player gets clips: null; portal/src/components/player/player.tsx:146-149 `voiceMissing = soundOn && narrator.voice === "missing"` and :450/:466 render VoiceNotice; portal/src/components/player/narrator.ts:62 decides from `engine.getVoices()` (no Azerbaijani voice on Chrome/Windows). docs/build/DECISIONS.md:161-172 ADR-028: 37,724 clips, 4.01 M chars, ~321 USD, ElevenLabs default voices retire 2026-12-31, voices must be chosen per language. docs/build/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md:7-9 Q2 open. No branch adds clips or touches the script (grep ELEVENLABS in *.diff: nothing outside .md).
- Smallest fix: No code change. Owner puts ELEVENLABS_API_KEY and ELEVENLABS_VOICE_AZ / _EN / _RU into portal/.env.local; run `npx tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/generate-narration.ts --locales az --only <module>/<lesson>` for one sample per language for the native reviewer, then `--locales az,en,ru --concurrency 4`; commit portal/content/narration/** and portal/public/generated/tts/** (or run the script in the Docker build before `npm run build`, as ADR-028 item 2 and README 'Narration voice' :279 describe). Other seven languages later with the same command.
- Files: portal/.env.local (owner, never committed), portal/content/narration/, portal/public/generated/tts/, portal/Dockerfile (only if generation moves into the image build)
- Risk: Repository size: ~37k mp3 files for ten languages (az/en/ru first is a third of that); consider the build-time step instead of committing. A wrong voice means regenerating that whole language (ADR-028 item 2 keys clips by voice). Cost is per run of new text only.
- Depends on: 
- Needs the owner: ELEVENLABS_API_KEY and plan; a native speaker per language to pick the voice (az, ka, ar first) after one sample lesson; budget approval (~30 USD per language, ~100 USD for az/en/ru).

### M-07 · high · open · effort XL
**No interoperability with customers' existing systems**

- Sources: audit:M-07, repo:REP-11, repo:OWN-4, docs:DOC-18
- Detail: [audit:M-07] No SCORM/xAPI export for LMSs (OPEN-QUESTIONS.md item 11), no SCIM provisioning, no LDAP sync (M-02), no public REST API; integrations are outbound only (webhooks and syslog).
  [repo:REP-11] Q11 asks whether SCORM/xAPI export is needed ('currently none'). training-pipeline.md §9 confirms: lessons exist only as the portal's JSON DSL in lesson_contents; no package export or LMS launch. The owner's strategic item 4 now answers yes (see OWN-4).
  [repo:OWN-4] No SCORM, xAPI or TinCan code exists: grep over portal/src, portal/scripts and content/library/modules.json returns nothing. Lessons live only as the portal's JSON DSL in lesson_contents (imported by syncLibrary in src/server/services/library.ts); the player is a React client component (src/components/player/player.tsx) that reports completion through server actions (learning.ts). The docs branch's API.md states there is no API-key REST API for other systems. OPEN-QUESTIONS Q11 and training-pipeline §9 record the gap.
  [docs:DOC-18] API.md section 1 line 20: 'There is no public REST API for machine clients. Every authenticated endpoint uses the browser session cookie ... There are no API keys, OAuth client credentials or service accounts.' Confirmed by the route list (every /api/admin and /api/me handler uses apiViewer/getViewer on the session cookie). Integrations are outbound only (webhooks, syslog). An HRIS or LMS cannot pull completion data or push people without a browser session, which also constrains owner item 4 (SCORM/LMS customers).
- Evidence: `grep -rliE 'scorm|xapi|scim|tincan' portal/src portal/scripts portal/content` returns nothing. Every route under portal/src/app/api (15 route.ts files listed) authenticates with apiViewer/getViewer/getSession on the session cookie or is a public token route (assets, health, qr, t/[token]/open); portal/src/server/auth/api.ts:12-20 apiViewer → getViewer() only; no bearer-token path exists. Outbound only: portal/src/server/services/events.ts:10-20 queues webhook/syslog rows into webhookDeliveries. The player imports server actions directly (portal/src/components/player/player.tsx:48-49 attestModuleAction, completeLessonAction, startLessonAction, setPreferencesAction), so it cannot run inside an LMS package as-is. Lessons exist only as lesson_contents rows (schema.ts:348-359) and content/library/lessons JSON (generate-narration.ts:22). docs/build/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md:22 Q11 still open; cloud-session-reports.md:48 owner item 4 asks for SCORM 1.2. No branch adds any of this.
- Smallest fix: Two separate pieces; do the cheaper one first. (A) Read-only reporting API: new table `apiTokens` (id = sha256(token) like sessions at schema.ts:206-209, tenantId, permission set, createdBy, lastUsedAt), an operator/admin action to mint one (settings-tabs Integrations card, admin.settings namespace), and in auth/api.ts:12 let apiViewer accept `Authorization: Bearer` by resolving the token to a Viewer with the tenant's permissions; the existing /api/admin/reports/[kind] (csv|xlsx, route.ts:15,35) and /api/admin/people/[kind] then serve machine clients unchanged; document in docs/API.md (docs branch). (B) SCORM 1.2 export (owner item 4): route portal/src/app/api/admin/modules/[id]/scorm/route.ts (apiViewer("studio.write")) that streams a zip (JSZip or node:zlib + a tiny zip writer, no new heavy dep) with imsmanifest.xml (one SCO per module), the module's lessonContents for the tenant locale as lessons.json, clips from public/generated/tts if present, and launcher.html + player bundle. The bundle needs a progress sink: add an optional `onProgress` prop to player.tsx replacing the four action imports at :48-49, and a script `portal/scripts/build-scorm-player.ts` (esbuild, already a Next transitive dep) that bundles components/player with a shim calling API.LMSSetValue("cmi.core.lesson_status"/"cmi.core.score.raw"/"cmi.core.session_time"). xAPI later from the same sink.
- Files: portal/src/server/db/schema.ts, portal/drizzle/<new migration>.sql, portal/src/server/auth/api.ts, portal/src/server/actions/settings.ts, portal/src/components/admin/settings-tabs.tsx, portal/messages/{az,en,ru,tr,ro,ka,uk,de,fr,ar}/admin.json, portal/src/app/api/admin/modules/[id]/scorm/route.ts, portal/src/components/player/player.tsx, portal/scripts/build-scorm-player.ts, docs/API.md
- Risk: (A) opens a new unauthenticated-by-cookie surface: tokens must be hashed, rate-limited (reuse rateLimit) and audited; CSRF-free since bearer. (B) a second build of the player drifts from the app's player; next-intl messages and Tailwind CSS must be bundled; lesson ids in answers/lessonProgress are not written back (LMS keeps completion), so portal reports will not see LMS learners unless the sink also posts to the reporting API.
- Depends on: M-10
- Needs the owner: Which LMS (SAP SuccessFactors, Cornerstone) to test the package in; whether LMS completions must flow back into the portal's reports; priority of SCORM vs SCIM vs reporting API for the first pilot.

### OWN-1 · high · open · effort L
**Market packs for de, fr, ar: local names, currency, government bodies and brand analogues**

- Sources: repo:OWN-1
- Detail: Today every language keeps the Azerbaijani world: lesson-engine.md recipe 6.3 (lines 1248-1250) requires 'Safarov Industries, manat/AZN, +994 numbers, Azerbaijani institutions' in all ten languages; 31 of the 106 de lesson files (same 31 in en) still mention manat/AZN. The brand registry content/library/brands.json has 169 entries with one `name` string each and no locale field (kinds: 55 app, 21 gov, 17 employer, 13 generic, 10 cloud/media/shop, 7 courier/utility, 5 payment, 4 bank/social, 3 telecom, 2 messenger, 1 hotel; 56 fakes with `imitates`); it is read at request time in src/app/(focus)/learn/[slug]/[lessonId]/page.tsx line 21 and drawn by src/components/player/brand-avatar.tsx. The name table lives in each glossary (.claude/skills/cyclowareness-experience/references/glossaries/{de,fr,ar}.md '## Character names'): its rule is to keep Azerbaijani spellings (Leyla Məmmədova, Rəşad Əliyev) in German/French/Arabic text. Catalogue titles per language are in content/library/i18n.{lang}.json. scripts/check-lesson-locales.ts enforces parity (ids, addresses, links unchanged), which a market pack must keep.
- Evidence: Confirmed as a deliberate decision, not an accident: docs/build/DECISIONS.md:148 (ADR-026 point 4: stories stay in the Azerbaijani company world in every language; a market with local stories 'means a separate decision and new lesson files') and .claude/skills/cyclowareness-experience/references/lesson-engine.md:1248-1250. Counts verified on main: 31 of 106 de lesson files mention manat/AZN, the same 31 in en, fr and ar; 35 de files contain +994. portal/content/library/brands.json: 169 entries, each with one `name` string, no locale field (kinds: app 55, gov 21, employer 17, generic 13, cloud 10, shop 10, media 10, courier 7, utility 7, payment 5, bank 4, social 4, telecom 3, messenger 2, hotel 1; 54 carry `imitates`, the finding said 56). Type portal/src/lib/content/types.ts:134-143 `name: string`. Loaded per request at portal/src/app/(focus)/learn/[slug]/[lessonId]/page.tsx:19-23 (allBrands) and filtered by brandRef at :26-37; displayed by portal/src/components/player/brand-avatar.tsx:75 (first letter fallback only) and portal/src/components/player/artifacts.tsx:266,304,322 (`a.brand ?? brand?.name`, `a.app ?? brand?.name`), so the visible brand name usually comes from the lesson's own translatable `brand`/`app` field (portal/src/lib/content/locale-parity.ts:35-39). Parity rules at locale-parity.ts:97-105: translatable keys may change freely, but every address token must stay (:100-103) and every other value must be identical. Addresses in the English lessons: 101 end in .example, 38 .net, 37 .az, 6 .com; campaign templates also use .az senders (portal/src/lib/campaigns/templates.ts:68). Glossary name tables as described: de.md:19-21, fr.md:9-10, ar.md:20-25. No branch touches this (docs.diff:1132 only lists brands.json).
- Smallest fix: Two tiers; only the first is small. Light market pack (no checker or schema change): (1) brands.json gets an optional `names?: Partial<Record<Locale,string>>` (types.ts:134-143) and page.tsx brandsFor() resolves `name: b.names?.[locale] ?? b.name` with the locale it already reads at :4 getLocale — three lines, avatar and artifacts unchanged; (2) a substitution pass over the 31 currency and 35 phone-prefix de/fr/ar lesson files in translatable keys only (say, spoken, text, body, subject, label, name, brand, app): manat/AZN → EUR for de/fr and the owner's chosen currency for ar, +994 → +49/+33/+9xx, institution names → local analogues, run with the existing docs/build/workflows/localize-language.js translator+editor pair and verified by `npx tsx scripts/check-lesson-locales.ts --coverage`, which already allows these edits; (3) the same pass over the L10n strings in src/lib/campaigns/templates.ts and src/server/lab/games.ts. People's names and every address (.az domains, e-mail addresses) stay, because locale-parity.ts:100-103 forbids changing them and a renamed person with an l.mammadova@ address would be worse than the current state. Full pack (local names, local domains) means reversing ADR-026: either new lesson ids per market (no parity) or a `MARKET_LOCALES` exemption in locale-parity.ts for address tokens plus a per-market address map; that is XL and a product decision.
- Files: portal/content/library/brands.json, portal/src/lib/content/types.ts, portal/src/app/(focus)/learn/[slug]/[lessonId]/page.tsx, portal/content/library/lessons/**/*.{de,fr,ar}.json (31 + 35 files), portal/src/lib/campaigns/templates.ts, portal/src/server/lab/games.ts, .claude/skills/cyclowareness-experience/references/glossaries/{de,fr,ar}.md, docs/build/DECISIONS.md (new ADR superseding ADR-026 point 4)
- Risk: Light pack: a learner in de reads EUR amounts next to an .az sender domain and Azerbaijani names (a mixed world); narration clips, if ever generated, are keyed by text hash so changed sentences need new clips; the parity checker catches structural damage but not style, so the editor pass is mandatory (ADR-026 point 3). Full pack: breaks the one-English-source parity model that every translation test relies on.
- Depends on: 
- Needs the owner: Target markets per language (de: DE/AT/CH; fr: FR/BE/CH/CA; ar: which country and currency), whether ADR-026 point 4 is reversed, native reviewers per market, and local brand analogues the owner is comfortable imitating (the 54 `imitates` fakes).

## tenant-admin-privacy (11)

### S-06 · medium · open · effort M
**Account-takeover tooling without step-up authentication**

- Sources: audit:S-06, security:L-7
- Detail: [audit:S-06] people.ts L183-L191 and L239-L250 (createLinkAction, resetTwoFactorAction): a tenant administrator can clear a fellow administrator's authenticator and mint a one-hour password-reset link for them; platform.ts L136-L147 (adminLinkAction): the platform operator can mint a reset link for any administrator of any organisation. Both are audited, neither needs re-authentication, a second approver or prior notice to the target. Insider and session-hijack risk; enterprise buyers expect break-glass governance.
  [security:L-7] createLinkAction (people.ts:183) lets a people.write administrator create a 60-minute password reset link for any person of their tenant, including another tenant_admin; resetTwoFactorAction (people.ts:239) removes that person's authenticator. Both are audited, but a 2FA reset leaves only an in-app notice seen after sign-in and a reset link leaves no notice at all. super_admin accounts are out of reach. Normal for many admin consoles, but banking/government customers may expect separation of duties.
- Evidence: Confirmed on main. portal/src/server/actions/people.ts:183-191 createLinkAction: actionViewer("people.write") then target() then issueAccountLink(u.id, kind) and audit; no password re-entry, no notice to the target. people.ts:239-250 resetTwoFactorAction: only guard is `u.id === v.user.id` (L242); clears totpSecret/totpEnabled/totpRecovery (L243), invalidates sessions, audits, inserts an in-app notification (L247) only. people.ts:40,45 reachable(): super_admin targets are excluded for non-super viewers, so the claim 'super_admin out of reach' holds. portal/src/server/actions/platform.ts:136-147 adminLinkAction: actionViewer("platform.manage"), target restricted to role tenant_admin and status active/invited (L142), issueAccountLink(u.id, "reset") (L144), audit only. No branch touches these three functions: grep of security/tests/demo/docs/audit .diff for resetTwoFactorAction|createLinkAction|adminLinkAction hits only prose in docs/SECURITY_REVIEW.md (security.diff:372). Reusable step-up pattern already exists: portal/src/server/actions/profile.ts:17-20 checkPassword(userId, password) (module-private) and policies.ts:58-60; portal/src/server/auth/password.ts:11-17 verifyPassword returns false for a null hash. PRIVILEGED_ROLES (permissions.ts:69) always sign in with a password, so every actor of these actions has a hash.
- Smallest fix: (1) Move checkPassword from profile.ts:17 into src/server/auth/password.ts as an exported verifyUserPassword(userId, password). (2) Add a `password: string` argument to resetTwoFactorAction (people.ts:239), createLinkAction for kind === "reset" only (people.ts:183; invite links for never-activated accounts stay as they are) and adminLinkAction (platform.ts:136); first line after actionViewer: `if (!(await rateLimit(`step-up:${v.user.id}`, 10, 15 * 60_000)).ok || !(await verifyUserPassword(v.user.id, password))) return { ok: false, error: "wrongPassword" }` (rateLimit from src/server/rate-limit.ts:54, same shape as learning.ts:75). (3) Add a password input to the confirm dialogs in src/components/admin/person-actions.tsx, people-client.tsx and platform-client.tsx (copy the password field of the profile password dialog). (4) Message keys admin.person.confirmPassword, admin.person.wrongPassword (and the same under the platform namespace used by platform-client.tsx) in all ten portal/messages/{az,en,ru,tr,ro,ka,uk,de,fr,ar}/admin.json. (5) Target notice: in resetTwoFactorAction and the reset branch of createLinkAction call notifyUsers(db(), v.tenant.id, [u.id], <new fixed kind>, {}) after adding one entry to FIXED_MESSAGES in src/server/services/notify.ts (NotifyKind = TemplateKind | keyof FIXED_MESSAGES, notify.ts:25). Second-administrator approval and a consented support-access grant are not part of the smallest change.
- Files: portal/src/server/auth/password.ts, portal/src/server/actions/profile.ts, portal/src/server/actions/people.ts, portal/src/server/actions/platform.ts, portal/src/server/services/notify.ts, portal/src/components/admin/person-actions.tsx, portal/src/components/admin/people-client.tsx, portal/src/components/admin/platform-client.tsx, portal/messages/*/admin.json, portal/tests/people-import.test.ts
- Risk: Signature change breaks every caller of the three actions (the three components above and any test calling them; grep showed no test on main). An admin who signed in through SSO-with-password-less flow cannot exist for PRIVILEGED_ROLES, but if that ever changes verifyPassword(null) returns false and the actions become unusable for them. The step-up rate limit must be keyed per actor, not per tenant, or one admin can lock out the others.
- Depends on: 
- Needs the owner: Whether peer-administrator actions need a second approver (separation of duties) and whether the operator's reset link should be replaced by a consented support-access grant; both are policy, not code, decisions.

### S-03 · medium · open · effort M
**Tenant isolation has a single layer**

- Sources: audit:S-03
- Detail: schema.ts: 51 tables with tenant_id on every tenant-owned table; 0000_init.sql has 0 row-level-security policies. Isolation is enforced by application predicates only; the review found them correct everywhere today (no cross-tenant read or write), but there is no automated cross-tenant test and no database-level backstop. One missed predicate in a future change becomes a cross-customer data breach; banks and agencies ask for defence in depth here.
- Evidence: Confirmed on main. `grep -il 'row level security|ENABLE ROW LEVEL|create policy' portal/drizzle/*.sql` matches nothing (exit 1); schema.ts has 34 `tenantId: tenantRef()` columns over 51 pgTable() calls (the rest are user-keyed or library tables). Isolation is application predicates only, e.g. people.ts:45 target() `eq(t.users.tenantId, v.tenant.id)`, signoffs route :16. No cross-tenant test on main: grep -i 'cross-tenant|other tenant|otherTenant|tenantB|second tenant' over portal/tests is empty. No branch adds RLS (no .sql in security/tests diffs; demo's 0001/0002 migrations are drill tables). The tests branch lays groundwork only: tests.diff:794-871 adds portal/tests/helpers/db.ts with testDb() (PGlite migrated from drizzle/) and an addTenant(db, overrides) factory, and tests.diff:2609 has one 'of another organisation' case for secops incidents, not a generated suite.
- Smallest fix: The test suite, not RLS: a new portal/tests/cross-tenant.test.ts built on tests/helpers/db.ts from the tests branch: create two tenants with addTenant, one admin viewer per tenant (the V type at tests.diff:1476 shows how learning-actions.test.ts stubs actionViewer), then for each tenant-scoped action in src/server/actions/{people,policies,assignments,campaigns,secops,settings}.ts and each route under src/app/api/admin/** call it as tenant A with tenant B's ids and assert { ok: false } / 404 and that no row of B changed. Start with the ~15 actions that take a bare id (people.ts target() callers, policies, campaigns) and extend. RLS proper (ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY + CREATE POLICY ... USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid) on the 34 tenant tables, a non-owner DB role in docker-compose, and wrapping every request in a transaction that runs SET LOCAL app.tenant_id) is an XL refactor because src/server/db exposes a module-level db() singleton, not a per-request transaction.

### D-05 · medium · needs_owner_decision · effort XL
**One email address can belong to only one organisation**

- Sources: audit:D-05
- Detail: schema.ts L198: users_email_idx on email alone; people.ts L121-L122. No consultants, group-company staff or managed-service partners across tenants; a tenant can squat addresses of a company that has not yet proven its domain; blocks the reseller/MSSP channel the pricing model counts on (25 % partner share).
- Evidence: Confirmed on main. schema.ts:198 uniqueIndex("users_email_idx").on(t.email) with no tenant column; people.ts:121-122 refuses any address already present in any tenant (deleted accounts included: the anonymised address at :319 is `deleted+<id>@invalid.local`, so a real address frees up on deletion). Domain squatting confirmed: people.ts:75-82 foreignVerifiedDomains only blocks domains another tenant has PROVEN (isNotNull(domainVerifiedAt)); an unproven company's addresses can be added by any tenant (:123, :528). Sign-in depends on uniqueness: auth.ts:218 `select ... from users where email = ?` returns one person per address, and platform.ts:45-46 refuses a tenant whose admin address exists anywhere. No branch changes the index or the sign-in lookup (demo.diff schema hunk only moves the line, tests.diff:2772-2789 tests createTenantWithAdmin as is).
- Smallest fix: Not a code defect: a product decision. If the owner wants multi-organisation people, the smallest workable shape is a `memberships` table (user_id, tenant_id, role, status, department_id, unique(user_id, tenant_id)) with users keeping identity fields only, users_email_idx unchanged, sessions.tenantId (schema.ts ~:210) chosen at sign-in via an organisation picker when a person has more than one membership, and every `eq(t.users.tenantId, ...)` predicate (grep shows dozens across src/server) rewritten to join memberships. That is the Roadmap 3.2 2.5-ew item, XL. The cheaper interim that closes only the squatting half: in people.ts:123 and :528 also refuse addresses whose domain belongs to a tenant with a domain set but not yet verified (drop isNotNull(domainVerifiedAt) from :80), S effort, but it lets an unverified tenant block others, so it needs the same owner call.
- Files: portal/src/server/db/schema.ts, portal/drizzle/<next>_memberships.sql, portal/src/server/auth/session.ts, portal/src/server/auth/viewer.ts, portal/src/server/actions/auth.ts, portal/src/server/actions/people.ts, portal/src/server/services/tenants.ts, portal/src/app/api/sso/callback/[tenant]/route.ts
- Risk: Touches sign-in, SSO auto-create, the viewer, every people query and the seed; a data migration must create one membership per existing user. Any missed predicate becomes a cross-tenant leak (ties to S-03's suite). The interim domain change can wrongly block a legitimate tenant whose domain another tenant typed without proving.
- Depends on: S-03
- Needs the owner: Decide whether one person may belong to several organisations before the first partner/MSSP deal, and whether email stays the sign-in identifier (vs. email + organisation picker).

### I-1 · info · fixed_on_branch (security) · effort S
**Notification placeholders could print inherited object members**

- Sources: security:I-1
- Detail: fill() in notify.ts looked up {{name}} placeholders on a plain object, so an admin template with {{constructor}} printed the source text of Object. Branch hunk: `(_, k: string) => (Object.hasOwn(vars, k) ? vars[k] : undefined) ?? ""`. Test sends a template with {{constructor}}{{toString}}{{__proto__}}{{hasOwnProperty}} and asserts the subject is ' for Aysel' and the text contains no 'function|native code|[object'. The only other {{...}} filler-like code is the LINK_TOKEN presence check in schemas/notifications.ts; tenant-defaults.ts only holds template strings.
- Evidence: Main checkout portal/src/server/services/notify.ts:13-15: `function fill(template, vars) { return template.replace(/\{\{\s*(\w+)\s*\}\}/g, (_, k) => vars[k] ?? ""); }` — `vars` is the plain object literal built at :79-87, so `{{constructor}}` resolves to `Object` and String.replace stringifies the callback result to "function Object() { [native code] }"; `{{__proto__}}` gives "[object Object]". The admin-editable template reaches fill() at :88 (subject), :90 (body) and :117 (in-app title). Defect confirmed on main; tests/email-escapes.test.ts on main has no inherited-key case (only the markup test at :31-38). security.diff fixes it: hunk at security.diff:733-744 changes notify.ts:14 to `(_, k: string) => (Object.hasOwn(vars, k) ? vars[k] : undefined) ?? ""` with the comment "Own keys only", and security.diff:767-786 adds a `describe("template placeholders")` test to portal/tests/email-escapes.test.ts that sends `{{constructor}}{{toString}} for {{name}}` / `{{__proto__}}{{hasOwnProperty}}Hi {{name}}` and asserts subject === " for Aysel", text not matching /function|native code|\[object/ and containing "Hi Aysel". `Object.hasOwn` already compiles on main (tsconfig lib esnext; used at src/components/lab/model/labs.ts:220). The only other `{{` handling in src/server and src/lib is the LINK_TOKEN presence regex at src/server/schemas/notifications.ts:6,15 and the DATED regex at notify.ts:39, neither of which looks values up, so no second filler needs the same fix. Branch worktree HEAD d59d677 (security).
- Smallest fix: None further: merge the security branch (notify.ts hunk + email-escapes.test.ts hunk). If the branch is cherry-picked partially, take those two hunks together.
